data:
Cameras, visual inspection and documents. CCTVService checks and describes camera sources and samples frames from them. SurveillanceService grades frames on the sovereign vision tier, detects objects locally at camera rate, keeps annotated evidence frames and streams events. MaterialAnalyticsService aggregates everything surveillance has seen. OCRService reads text, spreadsheet logic and source code out of documents.
The rule throughout is that an absence is reported as an absence. A frame nobody graded is not PRISTINE, a detector that did not score an object does not send 0.0, and every stage that might not run says what it did in a *_note field. Show those notes. Do not treat an empty list as “nothing there”.
data.analyzematerialquality#AnalyzeMaterialQu:
rpc AnalyzeMaterialQuality(AnalyzeMaterialQualityRequest) returns (AnalyzeMaterialQualityResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if exactly one of baseline_since and baseline_until is set. UNAVAILABLE if the sighting corpus or the baseline window cannot be read. Exploratory analysis over the sightings recorded by IngestSurveillanceFeed: which materials, object classes and sensors were seen, and how their damage grades are distributed. A comparison is returned only when you supply a complete baseline window.
The unit is a sighting, not a thing. A sighting is one object in one frame of one ingest. Nothing tracks an object between frames, so a six-frame sweep of two pallets yields twelve sightings. totals.multi_frame_sweep_sightings tells you how much of a result is exposed to that.
Absent is not zero. A sighting the vision tier did not grade is counted in ungraded_sightings and nowhere else. Means and shares are optional, each ships with its denominator, and they are absent when there is nothing to average.
Read corpus_scanned first. false means no scan happened, and every count is meaningless rather than zero.
data.boxorigin#BoxOrigin: Value Meaning BOX_ORIGIN_UNSPECIFIED No known stage assigned the box. This is not “no box”: check box_w and box_h. BOX_ORIGIN_VISION_GRADING The vision model’s scene-level grading turn. The weakest of the four. BOX_ORIGIN_VISION_DETECTION The vision model’s per-frame detection turn. BOX_ORIGIN_REGION_CLUSTERING Deterministic region proposal: “something is here”, with no label or grade. BOX_ORIGIN_LOCAL_DETECTOR A local detector in the serving process. Has detector_label. Never has a grade.

data.describesource#DescribeSource:
rpc DescribeSource(CCTVServiceDescribeSourceRequest) returns (CCTVServiceDescribeSourceResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if endpoint_url is empty. A device-capture camera pushes frames from the client, so the server has nothing to ask. UNAVAILABLE if the camera could not be asked. Asks the camera what it is instead of reading back what an operator typed. For rtsp:// and rtsps:// URLs the server speaks RTSP (OPTIONS, then DESCRIBE) and returns the session description the camera stated: its streams, codecs and so on. http(s):// URLs and file paths get a supported: false description that names what would answer for them. This is an answer, not an error.
A full description does not show that the camera is publishing usable video, that a frame would decode, or that playback would be permitted. A recorder will describe a channel whose camera is unplugged. Only sampling a frame answers that. Show the description’s reason verbatim.
data.detectedobject#DetectedObject:
One inspectable object located in a frame.
Field Type Description label string What the vision model says it is, for example pallet. Empty on the live path. material string What it is made of. Empty on the live path. damage_grade string This object’s grade: PRISTINE, DAMAGED or DEFECTIVE. Empty means not graded. damage_percentage int32 This object’s estimated damage, 0 to 100. box_x float Box left, 0 to 1 of frame width. box_y float Box top, 0 to 1 of frame height. box_w float Box width fraction. box_h float Box height fraction. item_match ItemMatch What this object is in your data. Unset when resolution was not requested, which is opt-in per deployment. label_in_vocabulary optional bool Whether label is in class_vocabulary. Absent: the classifier was not asked, so show no mark. true: object_class carries the member. false: out of vocabulary, and object_class is empty. object_class string The vocabulary member label resolved to. Countable. Set only when label_in_vocabulary is true. frame_index int32 Which sampled frame, 0-based. Meaningful only when frames_detected > 1. Objects are not tracked between frames. box_origin BoxOrigin Which stage produced the box. detector_label string The local detector’s class string, verbatim. Never copied into label and never mapped onto the class vocabulary. Empty when no local detector produced the object. detector_label_set string The label set detector_label comes from, for example coco.2017.80. detector_confidence optional float The detector’s score, 0 to 1, when it reported one. Absent means no score. A present 0.0 is a measured zero. It is not a probability that the label is right, and not a damage figure.
data.detectliveframe#DetectLiveFrame: rpc DetectLiveFrame(DetectLiveFrameRequest) returns (DetectLiveFrameResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if image_frame is empty or fails the same validation as IngestSurveillanceFeed. An undecodable frame is never reported as “nothing detected”. One frame in, the local detector’s boxes out, with no model and no network hop. Nothing is recorded: no lineage, no sighting, no evidence frame and no telemetry event. The frame is not downscaled. Every returned object has box_origin: BOX_ORIGIN_LOCAL_DETECTOR, a detector_label and a detector_label_set. Its label, material, damage_grade and object_class are empty, damage_percentage is 0 and label_in_vocabulary is absent. None of those is a finding, because nothing on this path grades.

Not a URL. captured_at google.protobuf.Timestamp When the frames were ingested. retained_until google.protobuf.Timestamp When FACE stops serving it. Not a deletion time. boxes_drawn int32 Rectangles drawn. 0 is a real answer. frame_index int32 Which sampled frame was drawn on, 0-based. One frame is retained per ingest. width int32 Image width in pixels. height int32 Image height in pixels.

Reads the first resolved file. With a language_hint other than empty or auto, it is parsed as source code. Otherwise the type comes from the extension: images and documents are refused, workbooks are treated as spreadsheet code, and anything else is parsed as source code.

data.extractknowledge#ExtractKnowledge: rpc ExtractKnowledge(CCTVServiceExtractKnowledgeRequest) returns (CCTVServiceExtractKnowledgeResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: UNAVAILABLE for an empty endpoint or a local webcam (0, webcam), which the server cannot capture. Frame acquisition errors are returned as they occur. Samples frames from the source and runs the local object detector on them. No vision model and no OCR is involved. The server tries the camera’s snapshot capability first when available, and falls back to decoding the stream. The frames come back as JPEG bytes, and text_summary reports the frame count, how the frames were obtained, and what the detector did and found.

UNAVAILABLE if the OCR engine is not enabled in this deployment. INTERNAL if the source cannot be resolved to files. OCRs every resolved file, PDFs and images, and joins the text with --- Start File: --- and --- End File: --- markers. A file that fails is marked --- Error Processing --- and skipped.

data.getevidenceframe#GetEvidenceFrame:
rpc GetEvidenceFrame(GetEvidenceFrameRequest) returns (GetEvidenceFrameResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. The frame must belong to the caller’s tenant. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION if the deployment has no evidence store, or the frame is past its retained_until. INVALID_ARGUMENT for a malformed handle. PERMISSION_DENIED if the handle belongs to another tenant. NOT_FOUND if the frame is not available. INTERNAL if the stored frame cannot be read. Returns the annotated JPEG an ingest retained, with FACE’s boxes and labels drawn in. The raw frame is never kept. A retained frame shows a reviewer what was assessed. It is not forensically provenanced: nothing signs it or timestamps it against a trusted clock, and a drawn box is FACE’s own model’s answer, not proof.
retained_until is when FACE stops serving the frame. It is not a deletion. The stored object stays until the storage lifecycle policy that the operator configures removes it.

The five graded buckets plus ungraded_sightings add up to the set’s sighting_count.
Field Type Description pristine_sightings int32 Graded PRISTINE. damaged_sightings int32 Graded DAMAGED. defective_sightings int32 Graded DEFECTIVE. destroyed_sightings int32 Graded DESTROYED. other_grade_sightings int32 A grade string that is none of the four, reported rather than folded into a neighbour. ungraded_sightings int32 No grade stated. data.ingestsurveillancefeed#IngestSurveillanc:
rpc IngestSurveillanceFeed(IngestSurveillanceFeedRequest) returns (IngestSurveillanceFeedResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if the request carries no usable input: no valid image_frame, no raw_ocr_payload, and no frames from feed_url. An image_frame that fails validation is reported as invalid image_frame. Inputs can be combined. The server uses:
image_frame: one JPEG or PNG. It is validated from its header before decoding (at most 12 MiB and 40 megapixels) and downscaled for the vision tier. raw_ocr_payload: text already read at the edge. feed_url: frames sampled from a feed. max_frames has the same default and cap as ExtractKnowledge. The vision model then grades the scene and names each inspectable object. People are never subjects. A frame holding only people, or nothing inspectable, is not assessed: the grade, classification, severity, remediation and damage percentage are all empty or zero, and that means “no finding”, not a low score. Per-object boxes come from a detection turn, region proposals or the local detector. objects[].box_origin says which.
Each ingest also:
records one sighting per object for MaterialAnalyticsService; emits a DAMAGE_ASSESSMENT telemetry event, or DAMAGE_ASSESSMENT_NOT_PERFORMED when the frame was not assessed; retains one annotated evidence frame, for the frame holding the worst object, only when the operator has configured a retention window. See evidence_note.

data.surveillanceservice#SurveillanceService:
Full name semantics.v1.SurveillanceService.
Two paths answer different questions at very different costs:
IngestSurveillanceFeed asks the sovereign vision model what is in the frame, what it is made of and how damaged it is. It can take minutes on CPU inference. It writes a lineage record and a sighting, may retain an evidence frame, and emits a telemetry event. DetectLiveFrame runs a local detector in the serving process and returns boxes in milliseconds. It grades nothing and writes nothing.
data.telemetryevent#TelemetryEvent: Field Type Description event_id string Event id. timestamp google.protobuf.Timestamp When it happened. event_type string DAMAGE_ASSESSMENT, DAMAGE_ASSESSMENT_NOT_PERFORMED or SENSOR_CUE. severity string SEVERE, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW. Empty for a frame that was not assessed. domain string LAND, AIR, MARITIME or CYBER, from the ingest. description string Human-readable summary. sensor_id string Originating sensor. damage_grade string Grade, when applicable. gps_coordinates string Location. metadata map For assessments: frames_processed, confidence_score, analysis_source. For cues: target_sensor_type, target_status, alert_payload. damage_percentage int32 Estimated damage, 0 to 100.
data.testconnection#TestConnection:
rpc TestConnection(CCTVServiceTestConnectionRequest) returns (CCTVServiceTestConnectionResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: UNAVAILABLE if endpoint_url is empty, or a file source does not exist or cannot be read. INVALID_ARGUMENT if an image file source does not decode. For rtsp://, http:// and https:// endpoints, the server probes the camera when a reachability probe is available in the deployment. Otherwise it accepts the endpoint without contacting it. Read success and live_check_performed together:
success live_check_performed Meaning true true The endpoint answered, or a file source exists and decodes. No video frame was decoded, so the stream itself is unverified. false true The probe ran and the endpoint did not answer. message says how. true false Nothing contacted the camera. This says nothing about reachability.
data.triggersensorcueing#TriggerSensorCueing: rpc TriggerSensorCueing(TriggerSensorCueingRequest) returns (TriggerSensorCueingResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if source_sensor_id or target_sensor_type is empty, or the target type is not one of INFRARED_CAMERA, YARD_CCTV or PLC_CRANE_LOCK. Broadcasts a SENSOR_CUE telemetry event with severity HIGH. No actuator is contacted: this service has no PTZ camera or PLC client. The status says a cue was requested.
data.vbamodule#VBAModule: Field Type Description name string Module name. code string Module code.
data.vocabularycounts#VocabularyCounts:
The three counts add up to the set’s sighting_count.
Field Type Description in_vocabulary_sightings int32 Label in the class vocabulary. out_of_vocabulary_sightings int32 Label graded and not in the vocabulary. not_asked_sightings int32 The classifier was not asked. Neither in nor out.
data.windowcomparison#WindowComparison: Field Type Description baseline_since google.protobuf.Timestamp Baseline window actually used. baseline_until google.protobuf.Timestamp Baseline window end. current_since google.protobuf.Timestamp Current window start. current_until google.protobuf.Timestamp Current window end. baseline_sighting_count int32 Sightings in the baseline. current_sighting_count int32 Sightings in the current window. material_deltas repeated GroupDelta One row per material present in either window. object_class_deltas repeated GroupDelta One row per class present in either window.

data: Web collection and CRM access. CrawlerService scrapes and crawls public web pages. MetasearchService runs the sovereign metasearch engine and exposes the prompt guardrail’s rule sets for inspection. HubspotService reads deals and contacts from HubSpot. All three run inside the FACE deployment: no third-party search or AI API is involved.
data.biasrule#BiasRule:
Used both for a rule that fired and for a rule in a rule-set listing.
Field Type Description rule_id string Rule id. description string What the rule checks. severity string CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW, verbatim from the rule. category string OWASP, OpenBias or DomainScope, verbatim from the rule. compliance repeated string Compliance standards the rule is cited under, for example ISO42001_AIManagerSystem or SOC2_AuditAndPrivacy. is_domain_scope bool true for a must-match (domain scope) rule. A hit on such a rule means the text fell outside the agent’s domain, not that it contained something forbidden. Display the two kinds differently.
data.connect#Connect: rpc Connect(HubspotServiceConnectRequest) returns (HubspotServiceConnectResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INTERNAL if the verification request cannot be built. Every other outcome is reported in success and message. Verifies api_key by making one read-only request to HubSpot. The key is not stored. For GetDeals and GetContacts to work, the operator must configure a HubSpot key on the deployment.
data.crawl#Crawl:
rpc Crawl(CrawlRequest) returns (CrawlResponse); Kind: Unary. The call returns when the crawl has finished. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if url is empty or not an absolute http(s) URL with a host, or if depth or limit is negative. If the call’s deadline passes or the call is cancelled mid-crawl, the matching status is returned (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED or CANCELLED). Crawls breadth-first from the seed. Only http and https links are followed. The crawl stops when limit pages have been attempted. The result is kept under the returned crawl_id in the serving process’s memory, for GetCrawlStatus.
depth counts link hops from the seed: the seed is at depth 0, and links are followed from any page whose depth is below depth. For example, depth: 1 fetches the seed and the pages it links to.
data.crawledpage#CrawledPage: Field Type Description url string Page URL. title string Page title. Empty on error. content_snippet string The first 500 bytes of extracted content, followed by ... when truncated. status string Success or Error.
data.evaluatebias#EvaluateBias: rpc EvaluateBias(EvaluateBiasRequest) returns (EvaluateBiasResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if agent_name is not a known rule set (the message lists the known names), or if text is empty or only whitespace. Checks text against an agent’s guardrail rule set without blocking anything, and reports every rule that fires. The enforcing guardrail stops at the first rule that fires. It uses the same matching, so this result matches what enforcement would do.
data.getcontacts#GetContacts: rpc GetContacts(GetContactsRequest) returns (GetContactsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: Same as GetDeals. Returns one page of contacts from HubSpot’s default page size.
data.getcrawlstatus#GetCrawlStatus: rpc GetCrawlStatus(GetCrawlStatusRequest) returns (GetCrawlStatusResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: None beyond authentication. An unknown crawl_id returns status: "Unknown" and no pages. Returns the pages recorded for a crawl. Crawl results are held in memory by the process that ran the crawl. They do not survive a restart and are not shared between replicas.
data.getdeals#GetDeals: rpc GetDeals(GetDealsRequest) returns (GetDealsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION if no HubSpot key is configured on the deployment. A HubSpot transport, HTTP or decoding failure is returned without a specific status code (clients see UNKNOWN). Returns one page of deals from HubSpot’s default page size, with the properties below.
data.hubspotcontact#HubspotContact: Field Type Description id string HubSpot contact id. firstname string First name. lastname string Last name. email string Email address.
data.hubspotdeal#HubspotDeal: Field Type Description id string HubSpot deal id. dealname string Deal name. amount string Amount, as HubSpot returns it. pipeline string Pipeline id. dealstage string Deal stage id. closedate string Close date, as HubSpot returns it.
data.hubspotservice#HubspotService:
Full name semantics.v1.HubspotService.
HubSpot access uses a key that the operator configures on the deployment. A key sent to Connect is only verified: it is never stored or used for later calls.
data.listbiasrules#ListBiasRules: rpc ListBiasRules(ListBiasRulesRequest) returns (ListBiasRulesResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if agent_name is not a known rule set. Returns the full rule set an agent’s prompts are checked against, so you can see what the gate checks without tripping it.
data.metasearchservice#MetasearchService:
Full name semantics.v1.MetasearchService.
This service returns only numbers that the search engine or the guardrail computed. It reports no invented score, ratio or percentage.
data.request-crawlrequest#Request: CrawlReque: Field Type Description url string Required. Seed URL. It must be an absolute http(s) URL with a host. depth int32 Maximum link hops from the seed. 0 means the default, 2. Capped at 5. limit int32 Maximum pages to attempt. 0 means the default, 10. Capped at 500. allow_external bool Follow links to other hosts. When false (the default), the crawl stays on the seed’s host or its subdomains, on the same port. This is a host rule, not a registrable-domain rule: with seed www.example.com, a link to example.com counts as external.
data.request-evaluatebiasrequest#Request: Eva: Field Type Description text string Required. The text to evaluate, such as a hypothesis, scenario name or search term. agent_name string The rule set to use. See Rule sets. Empty means HypothesisService. An unknown name is refused rather than silently falling back.
data.request-getcontactsrequest#Request: GetC: Field Type Description limit int32 Not applied by the server.
data.request-getcrawlstatusrequest#Request: G: Field Type Description crawl_id string The id returned by Crawl.
data.request-getdealsrequest#Request: GetDeal: Field Type Description pipeline_id string Not applied by the server. Deals from all pipelines are returned. limit int32 Not applied by the server.
data.request-hubspotserviceconnectrequest#Req: Field Type Description api_key string HubSpot API key or private-app access token. Write-only: never returned, logged or stored.
data.request-listbiasrulesrequest#Request: Li: Field Type Description agent_name string Same names, default and refusal as EvaluateBiasRequest.agent_name.
data.request-scraperequest#Request: ScrapeReq: Field Type Description url string Required. The page to fetch. render_js bool Render the page in a headless browser before extracting. The proto comment calls this reserved for future use, but the server implements it.
data.request-searchtermsrequest#Request: Sear: Field Type Description query string Required. The search query. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed. max_results int32 Ranked results to return. 0 or negative means 5. Capped at 20.
data.response-crawlresponse#Response: CrawlRe: Field Type Description crawl_id string Id for GetCrawlStatus. status string Completed, or Failed when at least one page was attempted and none was fetched. The call is synchronous, so the server never returns Started. pages_visited int32 Pages fetched successfully.
data.response-evaluatebiasresponse#Response:: Field Type Description agent_name string The rule set actually used, after the default was applied. rules_evaluated int32 How many rules the text was checked against. Read hits against this number. hits repeated BiasRule Every rule that fired, in evaluation order. Empty means the text passes. blocked bool true when the enforcing guardrail would refuse this text. Currently this is exactly “any hit”. Read this field rather than computing it from hits.
data.response-getcontactsresponse#Response: G: Field Type Description contacts repeated HubspotContact The contacts.
data.response-getcrawlstatusresponse#Response: Field Type Description status string Completed, Failed or Unknown. pages repeated CrawledPage Every page attempted, in visit order.
data.response-getdealsresponse#Response: GetD: Field Type Description deals repeated HubspotDeal The deals.
data.response-hubspotserviceconnectresponse#R: Field Type Description success bool true if HubSpot accepted the key. message string Outcome, including HubSpot’s HTTP status on rejection.
data.response-listbiasrulesresponse#Response:: Field Type Description agent_name string The rule set returned. rules repeated BiasRule The full rule set, baseline rules first. This is also the order in which a first-match refusal picks its rule.
data.response-scraperesponse#Response: Scrape: Field Type Description success bool Whether the page was fetched and extracted. url string The URL that was fetched. title string Page title. content string Main detected content, as Markdown or plain text. metadata map Not populated by the server. error_message string Why the scrape failed, when success is false.
data.response-searchtermsresponse#Response: S: Field Type Description query string The query as searched, echoed so responses can be matched to requests. results repeated SearchTermResult Ranked hits. There may be fewer than requested. requested_results int32 How many results the engine was asked for, after the default and cap were applied.
data.rule-sets#Rule sets:
agent_name accepts exactly these values:
AnalysisService, ClaimsService, ComplianceService, CopService, DocumentationService, FetchService, FinanceService, FulfilmentService, HypothesisService, PostureService, PredictiveMaintenanceService, ReverseLogisticsService, RulesService, SelfHealingService, SurveillanceService, TelemetryService, TwinsService, UnderwritingService, VisionService, VoiceService.
data.scrape#Scrape: rpc Scrape(ScrapeRequest) returns (ScrapeResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if url is empty. A page that cannot be fetched, or no free browser slot for render_js, returns success: false with error_message instead of an error. Fetches one page and extracts its title and main content. With render_js: true, the page is rendered in the server’s headless browser first, which waits for a browser slot. Otherwise it is fetched as plain HTML.
data.searchtermresult#SearchTermResult: Field Type Description title string Page title. url string Page URL. content string Clean readable text extracted from the page, truncated by the engine. Not a summary: no model has processed it. score double The engine’s relevance score for this hit. Comparable within one response only. Do not display it as a confidence or a percentage. image_url string A representative image for the page, when the engine found one.
data.searchterms#SearchTerms: rpc SearchTerms(SearchTermsRequest) returns (SearchTermsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if query is empty or only whitespace. UNAVAILABLE if the search fails. Runs a live search through the sovereign metasearch engine. The engine drives a headless browser, fetches and extracts candidate pages, then ranks them. This is an expensive call, not a typeahead: bind it to an explicit user action.
data.summary#Summary: Service RPC Kind Purpose CrawlerService Scrape Unary Fetch and extract one page CrawlerService Crawl Unary Crawl from a seed URL and record the pages CrawlerService GetCrawlStatus Unary Read a finished crawl’s pages MetasearchService SearchTerms Unary Ranked, content-extracted web search MetasearchService EvaluateBias Unary Check text against a guardrail rule set without blocking MetasearchService ListBiasRules Unary List a guardrail rule set HubspotService Connect Unary Verify a HubSpot key HubspotService GetDeals Unary Read deals from HubSpot HubspotService GetContacts Unary Read contacts from HubSpot

data:
The cockpit is FACE’s web app. Operators use it every day to ask questions of their data, review what the agents conclude, and approve or reject the actions the twins propose. FACE sends nothing to a third party until a person has approved it.
This section is a task guide, with one page per area. Text in bold is the exact wording on screen in the English interface.
data.other-tools#Other tools: Surveillance and CCTV Voice calls and the support log Document extraction Agent Orchestrator Connections and data sources
data.start-here#Start here: Sign in and choose an instance Navigation and Today's Command
data.the-four-stages#The four stages:
The bottom navigation follows FACE’s loop:
Reconcile what your systems do against your policies. Fetch answers from your data. Simulate what would happen. Act through the Twins. ReconcileMaturity and rules reconciliation FetchRuns, history, traces and schedules SimulateSwarm, metasearch and the causal matrix TwinsThe approval queue RemediationCompliance, finance and operations
data.your-account#Your account: Profile and billing Admin Accessibility and languages Troubleshooting

data.languages#Languages:
The cockpit is available in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. To change the language, go to PREFERENCES on your profile and choose from Target Language. The interface switches at once, and the choice is kept on this device.
The same setting also sets the language FACE writes its answers in. That covers fetch summaries and the twins’ analyses, so a French-speaking operator gets both the interface and the answers in French.
Some text is not translated: technical identifiers such as agent ids and fixed domain codes, and text that comes word for word from a server or a source system. The cockpit marks where a server’s own reply is shown, for example What this instance replied, in English:.
data.light-and-dark-themes#Light and dark the:
The cockpit has separate light and dark themes, each designed for contrast in its own right. It starts in the dark theme.
### Open your profile Select **User** in the bottom navigation. ### Find PREFERENCES Scroll to the **PREFERENCES** card. ### Switch the theme Next to **Theme**, select the button. It is labelled with the theme it switches to, **Light** or **Dark**, and its tooltip reads **Switch to the light theme** or **Switch to the dark theme**. This device remembers your choice.
data.screen-readers-and-the-keyboard#Screen r: Navigation. Each entry in the bottom navigation is a real button. It can take keyboard focus, shows a visible focus ring, and responds to Enter and Space. Screen readers announce its label together with whether it is the page you are on. Icon-only buttons. A button without a text label carries a tooltip and a spoken label. For example, the assistant button is announced as Open FACE AI assistant, and the ✕ on a twin card as a rejection that records a decision. Status changes. Errors and changing states are announced as they happen. These include the filter notice on Twins, a queue that failed to load, the reject dialog’s character counter, the call status (Call status: {status}), the camera report on CCTV, and the hand-off to Twins on Simulate. Charts. Charts that only restate figures already shown as text, such as the forecast chart on Simulate, are hidden from screen readers so the figures are not read twice. Reduced motion. When your system asks for reduced motion, the cockpit stops decorative animation, such as the pulsing status dot on Reconcile and the loading indicator’s partner rotation.
data.severity-is-never-colour-alone#Severity:
Neighbouring severity colours are too close to tell apart by colour alone, so every severity mark also has its own shape, and usually its word:
Severity Glyph Critical filled circle with an exclamation mark High warning triangle Medium square Low dash OK check mark Other states work the same way:
Rule verdicts on Reconcile pair a glyph with the words Aligned, Drift, Shadow, Missing and Unrated. Remediation banners and audit rows print their status word beside the glyph. A selected filter chip on Twins shows a check mark. Priority chips always print the priority word.

data:
Admin (/admin) manages who can use an instance and with which role. The Admin entry appears in the bottom navigation, just before User, only when the server reports that you are an admin of the selected instance. Anyone else sees their role as a badge in that place (Your role on this instance: {role}). The server checks your role again on every call, so the page cannot be used by someone without it.
Roles are Admin, Editor and Viewer.
data.invite-someone#Invite someone: ### Enter the address Under **Invite someone**, type the person's **Email address**. ### Pick the role Choose **Admin**, **Editor** or **Viewer** under **Role**. The default is **Viewer**. ### Select Invite **Invited {email} as {role}.** confirms the invitation. The person can then sign in and choose this instance. If you have not chosen an instance yet, the page shows the instance picker first. Only an admin of this instance can manage its members. means your role on the selected instance is not Admin.
data.members-and-roles#Members and roles:
The list shows every person who holds a grant on the instance. You marks your own row. You cannot change your own access. A row marked Pending has been filed and applies when the platform reconciles.
Change role lets you pick a new role, then Save. Remove asks Remove {email} from this instance? They lose access on their next request. Confirm with Remove access. No person holds a grant on this instance means the list was read and is empty. Service accounts are counted but not listed.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: runink.ui.access.v1.AccessService: ListMembers, InviteMember, SetMemberRole, RemoveMember. See the API reference.

data.rpcs-behind-these-pages#RPCs behind thes: CallingService.Signal, EndCall. SupportService.RecordSupportEvent, ListSupportLog. See the API reference.
data.support-log#Support Log:
The Support log button in the calling page’s title bar opens Support Log (/support_log). It lists one card per call, newest first. Each card shows the call id, the source, the start time, the duration and the number of entries. The call in progress is marked Live.
Every turn and call event is written to the log, for example Call started and Microphone muted. What this console keeps at the top of the page states what is retained:
Voice-call transcripts are stored on the server and survive a restart. Call audio is transcribed as it arrives and then discarded. No recording is kept, so there is nothing to play back. SMS and WhatsApp messages are not recorded. Copy as Markdown copies the whole log. The copy button on a card copies that one call. With nothing to show, the page reads No interactions recorded yet.
data.talk-to-face#Talk to FACE:
The calling page (/calling) opens a live voice conversation with FACE’s voice agent in your browser. To open it, go to Today’s Command and select Voice chat in the AI Command bar.
The page states This call is recorded and transcribed for control and quality purposes. The transcript is kept with this session for reference.
### Start the call Select **Start call**. Allow microphone access when your browser or device asks. The status line reads **Connecting…**, then **In call — listening**. ### Speak The transcript fills in as you talk, with each turn labelled **Caller** or **Agent**. While the agent answers, the status reads **Agent speaking…**. ### Interrupt, mute or hang up - **Stop the agent** cuts the agent off in the middle of a reply. - **Mute microphone** / **Unmute microphone** switches your microphone off and on. - **End call** hangs up. Leaving the page also ends the call. The status is announced to screen readers as Call status: {status}. The possible values are Ready to call, Connecting…, In call — listening, Agent speaking…, Call ended and Call failed. When a call fails, the reason appears under the status.

data: FACE reads your data only through the connections you configure. This page covers the cockpit side. For each connector’s settings, see Data sources.
data.add-a-connection-from-this-page#Add a co:
New connection opens a three-step wizard: Source, Runner, Review.
Pick a source card from the server’s catalog and fill in its fields. Choose the runner. Review, then select Test & save, or Save if you turned off Test after saving. For database sources, you also choose the encryption in transit. The strictest option is Encrypt, verify the chain and the hostname. Use it unless the source cannot support it.
data.connect-a-data-source#Connect a data sou:
CONNECT DATA SOURCE (/connect_data_source) is FACE’s own three-step wizard. To open it, select New connection on Fetch, or Other source types on Connections. When you return to Fetch, the new source is already selected.
### Step 1/3: pick the source and enter its details Select a source card. Each card is announced as **Select {name} source**. The cards are: - Databases and warehouses: Snowflake, Databricks, PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery. - Files and object storage: Excel, Object Store. - Business applications: Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Guidewire, Hubspot. - Documents, video and the web: PDF, Google Docs, Video Stream, Webpage. - Logistics systems: Inventory, OMS, TMS, IMS, YMS, ERP, CRM, WHS. - Devices and telemetry: MQTT Bus, RFID Reader, GPS Telematics, Sensor Gateway. The form below the cards depends on the source. Many sources use the general fields: **CONNECTION NAME**, **USER**, **PASSWORD** and **HOST / ENDPOINT**. PostgreSQL and MySQL add **DATABASE** and **ENCRYPTION IN TRANSIT**. Snowflake and Databricks can also take a whole connection string: turn on **PASTE A CONNECTION STRING** and paste it into **CONNECTION STRING**. The string is write-only. ### Step 2/3: choose the compute runner Under **TARGET COMPUTE RUNNER**, choose between two options: - **Runink Managed** is the recommended default. Runink runs the reads on the platform's own fetch runner, which is reached over mutual TLS, and the credential is sealed to it for each fetch. - **Self-Hosted Runner** means your own Kubernetes cluster or VM, which needs manual setup. Select **NEXT STEP →**. **← Back to Credentials** returns you to step 1. ### Step 3/3: review and save Check the summary, which is marked **Read-only Access**. A pasted connection string shows as held, not shown. Then select **Save & Finalize →**. After you save, the cockpit creates the connection and tests it:
You see Meaning Connection Successful The source answered and accepted the credentials. It does not mean data has been read. Configuration saved The connection is saved, but no live check exists for this source type, so nothing here says the source is reachable. The connection was NOT saved: {reason} Nothing was stored. Connection test failed: {message} The connection was saved, and the test failed. On success the wizard closes by itself.
data.connections--runners#Connections \u0026a:
To open Connections & Runners (/connections), go to Fetch and select the ACTIVE CONNECTIONS heading. The page has three tabs:
Active Connections: the connections themselves. The estate map. Compute Runners: the runners that execute reads. Other source types, in the title bar, opens FACE’s own connect wizard. Use it for video streams, documents and web pages.
data.rpcs-behind-these-pages#RPCs behind thes: runink.ui.datasources.v1.ConnectionsService: ListConnectionTypes, ListConnections, CreateConnection, UpdateConnection, RotateCredentials, DeleteConnection, TestConnection. ListenersService and RunnersService. semantics.v1.ConfigService.CreateConnection and TestConnection, for the FACE wizard. CrawlerService.Scrape. See the API reference.
data.the-connection-list#The connection list:
Each row shows:
the connection’s name, type and id; where it runs: Runink managed or runs on {runner}; a credential chip: credential stored, no credential needed, no credential, credential unreadable or credential state not reported; the result of the last test, if there was one. A stored credential is never shown. Its chip only says that a credential is held. It doesn’t say that the source will accept it.
The row buttons are:
Edit Rotate credentials Test Listener Delete Test asks first. It opens a connection with the stored credential on the connection’s runner. The test is read-only and time-limited, nothing is read from the source, and the attempt is audited. Delete also asks first, because it deletes the credential bundle as well, and a deleted bundle cannot be recovered. If other connections share the bundle, the confirmation names them.
You see Meaning The connections were not read The request failed. This is not an empty list. The connection registry could not be read The server answered but could not read its registry. No connections yet The registry was read and holds no connections. Use New connection to add the first one. Tested: the source answered… The source is reachable. It does not mean data has been read. Nothing was tested: this connector has no reachability check. Reachability is unknown, not confirmed.
data.web-scraper#Web scraper: Add Web Scraper, beside ACTIVE CONNECTIONS on Fetch, opens Web Scraper Setup (/crawler_connection). Enter a Target URL and select Test Scrape to see the first part of the page’s content as FACE’s crawler reads it. The page has no bottom navigation. Use the back button to leave it.

data: Fetch Center is where you ask your data a question. You can type it, dictate it or attach files to it. It runs against the sources you select, and the answer comes back as Twin Insights. Open it with Fetch in the bottom navigation (/fetch).
data.compute-runners#Compute runners: COMPUTE RUNNERS lists the runners registered for the instance. Runs use the managed runner, which is marked Active. Other runners show Standby.
data.create-a-schedule#Create a schedule: ### Open the form Select **CREATE NEW SCHEDULE**. The form is titled **SCHEDULE FETCH** — **Automate Data Discovery**. ### Pick the task Under **TASK CONFIGURATION**, choose a **FETCH TOPIC** from the fetch starters and a **RUNNER TYPE**. A scheduled run always executes on the managed runner. ### Pick the frequency Under **RECURRENCE LOGIC**, choose **DAILY**, **WEEKLY** or **MONTHLY**. **NEXT RUN** shows when it would next run. ### Save Select **SAVE SCHEDULE**. **Schedule Saved Successfully** closes the form. **Could not save the schedule. It was not created.** means nothing was stored. Scheduled runs send no alerts. The form says so under NOTIFICATIONS. To be told when a run ends, turn on Call Me When Finished or WhatsApp Me for a run you start yourself.
data.decision-artifacts#Decision artifacts:
A decision artifact is the full record of one proposed action, with the drafts it would produce: an email, a calendar invite, an ERP change. Open one from a Twins card:
View full decision artifact opens a preview, marked PENDING. Approve All approves the action. Approving a card that has artifacts opens the outcome, marked QUEUED. The footer reads Action approved — queued for execution. The page shows DECISION ARTIFACT #{id}, the title, the decision trail and the GENERATED DRAFTS. A link that carries no decision shows No decision artifact.
data.execution-history#Execution history:
EXECUTION HISTORY lists your runs, newest first. The automatic session fetch is listed here too. Each run card shows the command, the result or error, the duration, Runner: and Connections:, and a provenance badge. The badge reads Live, Cached, Offline — queued, Low confidence or Failed.
Reuse Prompt runs the same command again. Delete Execution removes that one run, after you confirm Delete this run?. Clear Log clears the whole history, after you confirm Clear Execution History. Run history is stored on this device.
Below the runs are traces: the lineage datasets FACE has recorded, with the schema and how fresh each one is. Tap a trace to open its details: rows, size, freshness, columns, downstream datasets and the description.
data.open-a-past-run#Open a past run:
Tap a run card to open Fetch details (/fetch/run/). It shows:
the status: Completed, Failed or Queued offline; Query, Runner, Connections, Started and Duration; Error, when there was one; Result; What happened to the sources: notices about individual sources, word for word; AI analysis; Generated SQL. Reuse Prompt in the title bar returns to Fetch Center and runs the command again. This run is no longer in your history. means the run was deleted or the history was cleared.
data.other-pages-linked-from-fetch#Other page: ACTIVE CONNECTIONS (the heading) opens Connections. New connection opens the connect-a-data-source wizard. Document Extraction opens OCR. CCTV Connection opens CCTV. Add Web Scraper opens the web scraper. Agent Orchestrator opens the orchestrator.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: FetchService.RunFetchStream (server stream), ListFetchStarters, ListTraces, GetTraceDetails. ConfigService.ListConnections, ListRunners. SchedulesService.ListSchedules, CreateSchedule, UpdateSchedule, SetScheduleActive, DeleteSchedule. ModelService.SpeakFetchSummary, SynthesizeSpeech. TwinsService.ExecuteAction, for Approve All. See the API reference.
data.run-a-fetch#Run a fetch:
### Choose your sources Under **ACTIVE CONNECTIONS**, tap a source card to include or exclude it. The caption reads **Included in fetch** or **Not included**. It describes your selection. It does not say whether the source is reachable. When the connection list loads live, every configured source starts out included. ### Ask your question Type in **Ask a question or use voice command…**, or tap a card under **FETCH STARTERS** to fill the box with a prepared question. To add input, use the buttons beside the box: - **Voice Input** dictates. Dictation stops after a pause and the fetch starts by itself. - **Camera Input** attaches a photo. - **Attach File** attaches one or more files. Attachments appear as chips that you can remove. ### Choose how to be told **Call Me When Finished** and **WhatsApp Me** ask FACE to notify you when the run ends. ### Run it Press Enter or select **Run Fetch**. A progress dialog, **Analyzing your data…**, lists each step as the server streams it. A finished step gets a check mark. The dialog shows **Ready** and closes when the run ends. ### Read the answer Under **Twin Insights**, the spoken summary comes first, followed by the cards. The summary is also read aloud. A photo taken with Camera Input is also offered to the surveillance pipeline. The snackbar tells you which of three things happened: the photo was offered, the offer failed, or it was attached to the prompt only. The photo is listed under Captured media on Reconcile.
If the cockpit cannot reach the server, the run is queued on your device (Offline mode: Fetch task queued for background synchronization.). It runs when the connection returns.
data.schedules#Schedules:
Fetch Schedules, in the link row above the history, opens Active Schedules (/active_schedules). The subtitle counts the tasks, for example 2 OF 3 TASKS RUNNING.
The filter menu (Filter Tasks) offers All, Active only and Paused only. Each card shows ACTIVE or PAUSED, FREQUENCY, NEXT RUN and LAST RUN. The switch (Toggle schedule status) pauses or resumes the schedule. Edit Schedule opens the schedule form. Delete Schedule asks Delete schedule? before it deletes. CREATE NEW SCHEDULE opens a blank form. No schedules match this filter. means the list loaded and nothing matched. A failed load shows the error instead.
data.the-status-line#The status line:
The banner at the top says where you stand, and it offers the next step:
You see Button A fetch is running… Checking your configured sources… Could not load your data sources., with the transport error Retry No data source is configured yet. Connect a data source Sources are configured, but no fetch has run on this device yet. Ask your first question Your last fetch failed. Open the run Your last fetch is queued offline and has not run yet. Open the run Your last answer came back low-confidence. Ask again Your last answer was reused from cache, not fetched live. Ask again Your last fetch succeeded. Ask a new question Could not load your data sources. means the cockpit could not look. No data source is configured yet. means it looked and found no sources.
data.twin-insights#Twin Insights: Card Shows Decision The recommendation, a {percent}% confidence badge, and Why:, Plan: and Risks: lines. Recommended Action A priority badge and Impact:. Forecast Forecast:, and an ANOMALY badge where one was detected. Signal Its source and Relevance:. Each proposed action is judged before it reaches you. A decision or action card that was judged carries a footer: Judgement: followed by concurs, dissents, unable to judge — not agreement or out of scope — not judged, then the judge’s reason. assessed by the model or checked without a model says how the verdict was reached. An action the judge dissented from is removed from the answer and listed under Actions rejected, with a count of how many actions it concurred with, dissented from, or could not judge.

data.the-bottom-navigation#The bottom navigat:
Every page after sign-in has the same bottom bar:
Entry Opens Also lit while you are on Reconcile Reconcile Fetch Fetch Center schedules, connections, the connect wizard, CCTV, document extraction, the orchestrator and surveillance Simulate Simulate Twins Actionable Twins the remediation screens, decision artifacts and Today’s Command Admin Admin Shown only to an admin of the selected instance. Other people see their role as a badge in the same place. User User Profile billing The bar is keyboard-operable. Each entry is a button that screen readers announce with its label and its selected state.
Right after you choose an instance, the cockpit starts a session fetch in the background. This is the first reading of your data. When it completes, the compliance, finance and operations twins run on its findings and the rules are read again. That is why Twins and Reconcile fill in without you starting anything. The session fetch runs once per session, whichever page you open first.
data.the-face-ai-assistant#The FACE AI assist:
The round button with the Runink mark, at the bottom right of every page, opens the assistant. Its tooltip is FACE AI, and screen readers announce it as Open FACE AI assistant.
The panel suggests prompts that fit the page you are on. For example, on Fetch or Connections it offers Create new connection and Find extra docs. On any other page it offers Help me with this screen and What can I do here?. Your prompt is sent together with the name of the page you are on.
Control Label Text box Ask FACE… Send Send message Microphone Start Recording / Stop Recording. Your speech is submitted when you stop. Camera Take a photo Attachment Attach a file Your question appears as You asked: {question}, followed by the assistant’s rationale and recommendation. FACE AI could not answer means the request failed, and the reason follows it. No answer came back means the assistant finished but returned nothing to show.
If voice input is blocked, the panel says Voice input is unavailable in this browser or the microphone was blocked. Type your question instead.
data.todays-command#Today\u0026rsquo;s Comman:
Command View (subtitle Daily Ops Briefing) is a one-page briefing. Open it from the Twins page: select Today’s Command, the last chip under ACTIONABLE TWIN STATUS. The back arrow (Go back) returns you to Twins.
The headline card offers two buttons:
Run Fetch runs a trace that ranks business risks and opportunities. If the server refuses the run, its reason is shown in the card. View Last Trace opens Fetch. The AI Command bar takes a typed or spoken instruction (Ask or command…, with Voice input and Send). Read aloud speaks the answer. The bar also has two shortcuts: Video opens Surveillance, and Voice chat opens a voice call.
The four sections below the bar each link to the stage they summarise:
Section Shows Link 1. SYSTEM POSTURE (Health & Context) Each data domain’s grade, alerts and maturity. View Data Posture Center → 2. BUSINESS LOGIC & RISKS (Rules Recon) Ranked risks and opportunities, once a fetch has run. View Rules Recon → 3. ACTIVE HYPOTHESES (Simulation) Ranked risks and opportunities, once a fetch has run. View Simulate → 4. DECISION TWINS (Actions) The decisions you approved in Twins, grouped by category. View Twins → Empty sections explain themselves:
Not assessed means no grades exist yet. Nothing is connected yet means no data source is attached. Connect one from Connections. No decisions yet means you should run a fetch to have the twins analyse your data. Nothing approved yet means you have not approved anything in Twins yet. What evidence did you use? opens a drawer. It shows the trace id, how many inferred domains and data objects were analysed, and the sources. Before any analysis has run, it says No analysis has run in this session yet, so there is nothing to evidence.
Behind this view: FetchService.RunFetch, PostureService.GetHealthScore, TwinsService.GetActionQueue and ModelService. See the API reference.

data:
Document Extraction (/ocr) reads a document on the server. It returns either the document’s text or the structure of the source code in it. To open it, go to Fetch and select Document Extraction beside ACTIVE CONNECTIONS.
### Choose a mode Select **Text** to extract prose, or **Code** to extract source-code structure. Changing the mode clears the previous result. ### Point to the document Enter the **Document path**, for example `/path/to/file.pdf`. The server reads the file at this path, so it must be a document the FACE server can open. Choose a **Format**: AUTO, PDF, DOCX or PPTX. ### Extract Select **Extract**. The button stays disabled until a path is entered.
data.results#Results:
Text mode shows Extracted text, with a confidence pill. The pill shows the confidence when the server measured it, and Confidence not measured otherwise. Code mode shows Language:, the number of functions and classes, and the code. Before the first extraction the page says Enter a document path and extract. No text extracted. means the document was read and held no text. A failed request shows its error instead.
Behind this page: OCRService.ExtractText and ExtractCode. See the API reference.

data:
Agent Orchestrator (/orchestrator) hands a task to one agent. The agent works through it in a loop: it thinks, acts, then observes the result. You watch each iteration arrive. To open it, go to Fetch and select Agent Orchestrator in the link row above the execution history.
### Choose the agent Pick an id from the **Agent** list, for example `twins`, `claims`, `compliance` or `reverse_logistics`. The default is `twins`. ### Describe the task Type it in **Command** (**Describe the task for the agent…**). ### Run Select **Run**. The button becomes **Stop** while the loop runs. Select **Stop** to stop following the run.
data.reading-the-loop#Reading the loop:
Each iteration appears as a numbered card with Thought, Action and Observation. Its status is a word as well as a colour:
Thinking Executing Observing Done Failed Iteration limit reached Not started When the loop ends in Done, Final result shows the agent’s answer. A run stops after eight iterations at most. Before the first run the page reads Issue a command to start the agent loop. A failed request shows the server’s message.
Each proposed action in the agent’s final answer is judged before it is accepted. See the judgement notes on Fetch.
Behind this page: RalphOrchestratorService.ExecuteLoop (server stream). See the API reference.

data.billing--usage#Billing \u0026amp; Usage:
Billing & Usage (/billing) is the shared billing page. The same content is shown on your profile under Plan & usage.
A banner names the payment provider. FACE configures none, so on FACE it always says Billing is not configured on this deployment. Plans and prices are shown for reference; no payment can be taken here. The subscription card shows the plan and its status: Active, Trial, Payment overdue, Canceled, Unpaid or Awaiting payment. It also shows seats, the billing interval, the period end and the price. Manage billing opens the provider’s portal. Usage shows each meter against its allowance. A meter can read Not measured or Unavailable. On FACE the compute-unit meter reads Not measured, with the reason. Estimate — not a charge appears when the server sends an estimate. Plans lists the plans with their prices (see Plans and billing). You can choose seats (Add a seat, Remove a seat) and Bill yearly. Continue to checkout stays disabled while no payment provider is configured. Readers and service accounts can’t start a checkout or open the billing portal. No subscription is on record for this account. means the record was read and is empty. The subscription record could not be read. This does not mean there is no subscription. means the request failed. Select Retry.
data.compute-units-cu#COMPUTE UNITS (CU):
This section is the tenant’s self-managed compute budget: a ceiling you set. It shows the DEDICATED (the ceiling), CONSUMED and REMAINING compute units. While REMAINING is 0, a fetch is refused before it runs and asks you to top up here. Under SET DEDICATED CU, pick 250, 500, 1000 or 2000, or enter a custom amount. Readers can’t change it. The PAYMENT RAIL shows whether card payment is connected.
The budget is not your plan’s CU allowance, and DEDICATED here does not mean the Dedicated plan. Fetches no longer add to CONSUMED: it keeps what earlier releases recorded, and model time is metered per billing account instead (see Plans and billing).
The readout tells three cases apart:
You see Meaning Measuring… The budget has not answered yet. Unavailable The budget did not load, so nothing is a measurement. Not measured No budget has been read yet.
data.instances#Instances: Instances lists the instances you hold a grant on, with your role, the plan and its status, and how long your access lasts: Access until {date}, Access does not expire (the grant sets no end date), or Access expiry not stated. To switch instance, return to the instance picker.
data.integrations#INTEGRATIONS:
The integration fields are:
WhatsApp Phone Number Stripe API Key Phone Number SMS Phone Number Google Credentials (Gmail, Drive) Google Analytics ID The edit button (Edit {label}) changes a value. A secret shows only Configured (hidden) or Not Set. When you edit a secret, the box starts empty: enter a new value to replace the stored one. The stored value is never shown.
data.plan--usage#Plan \u0026amp; usage: Plan & usage is the billing page’s content, shown in place: your subscription, each usage meter against its allowance, and the plans. It is the only place the profile shows usage. A meter that was not measured says so (Not measured, Unavailable) instead of showing a figure. See Plans and billing.
data.preferences#PREFERENCES: Theme switches between the light and dark themes. The button is labelled with the theme it switches to. The cockpit starts dark, and this device remembers your choice. Target Language sets the interface language (English, French, Spanish or Portuguese). It also sets the language that fetch answers and the twins are written in. Offline answers says whether this device can answer offline.
data.rpcs-behind-these-pages#RPCs behind thes: runink.ui.profile.v1.ProfileService: GetProfile, ListInstances, EndAllSessions. MeteringService: GetComputeBudget, SetComputeBudget. ConfigService: GetIntegrationConfig, SetIntegrationConfig. runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService: GetOverview, ListPlans, QuotePlan, StartCheckout, OpenPortal. See the API reference.
data.sessions#Sessions: Sign out ends this session. Sign out everywhere ends every session of yours on every device, this one included. Confirm with Yes, sign out everywhere. The page then says how soon every server honours it (within a few seconds).
data.user-profile#User Profile: Select User in the bottom navigation to open User Profile (/profile). The refresh button reads everything again, and As of {time} shows when the page was last read.
data.who-you-are#Who you are:
The identity card lists your Email, Name, Signed in with, Role, Platform admin, Tenant and Account ID. A value the server did not provide reads Not provided. A value the page could not read reads Not read, and its tooltip gives the reason.
Signed in with is Google account, Password (with your two-factor code when you use one) or API key (not a person). A session started before FACE recorded the method reads Not stated; sign in again to see it.
data.your-data-your-call#YOUR DATA, YOUR CALL: This section explains how to leave with your data. Close account & take my data explains the closure process. Open-source licences lists the licences of the software the cockpit includes.

data: Reconcile compares what your systems actually do with what your policies say they should do. It also grades how mature each business domain is. Open it with Reconcile, the first entry in the bottom navigation (/ai_center). The page is titled Business domain value reconciler, under the line CODE VS POLICY RECONCILIATION.
data.maturity--rules-reconciliation#Maturity:
The command bar at the top of Executive briefing gives two readouts side by side:
AI maturity: a ring showing the mean level across the domains, as L{level} / {max} on a 1–5 scale. It shows Not assessed yet before any assessment. Rules state: a bar that splits the rules by verdict, with a legend giving each count and state. The {count} invariants badge counts the rules. The domain pills under the bar, starting with All domains ({count}), narrow the rules list further down the page. They don’t change the two readouts. Tap the selected pill again to clear it.
data.operator-deep-dive#Operator deep dive: Domain posture console shows six gauges: Quality, PII risk, Lineage, Freshness, Policy and Cost. Each is the mean of the domains that measured it. A gauge with no measurements reads not measured. Live agent activity shows the steps the agents emitted, newest first. You can pause, resume or clear the buffer. LIVE or PAUSED shows its state. The activity stream is not connected. means there is no stream. No agent steps yet on this connection. means the stream is connected and quiet. Rules Recon lists every rule: Per-domain cards with TOTAL RULES and a bar by verdict. Tap a card to filter by that domain. The Logic Discovery Stream chips (All, Aligned, Drift, Shadow, Missing, Unrated) filter by verdict. The verdict banner. When rules have drifted or are missing, Review what drifted jumps to them. Review the undocumented does the same for shadow rules. Tick rules and select Send to Simulate to ground our hypothesis to use them in a simulation. While the agent reads, the list shows AGENT ORCHESTRATION IN PROGRESS. No business rules have been discovered yet. means the extraction answered with no rules. Failed to extract rules: {error} means it could not run, and Retry asks again.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: PostureService.GetHealthScore. RulesService.AnalyzeCode, UpdateRulePolicy. LineageService.GetSourceActivity. ConfigService.ListConnections. ActivityService.SubscribeAgentActivity (server stream). See the API reference.
data.rule-verdicts#Rule verdicts:
Every rule carries one verdict. Each verdict has its own glyph and word as well as its own colour, so it never depends on colour alone.
Verdict Glyph Meaning Aligned circled check Aligned with policy. Drift octagon Drifted: needs reconciliation. Shadow circled exclamation mark Undocumented. Missing warning triangle Missing: needs reconciliation. Unrated question mark The agent returned no verdict. The rule is not yet reconciled.
data.sections#Sections: Section What it holds Cross-domain relational matrix Starts collapsed; tap to expand. A table of each domain’s Grade, Quality, PII risk, Lineage, Freshness, Policy and Cost, then the relationships the agent reported, word for word. A chord ring draws the domains and their links. Tap a domain on the ring to scope the sections below it to that domain, and tap it again to clear. Object provenance The quality and risk checks recorded for each domain. Data communities The communities found in your data beside your source inventory, grouped by kind of source. The notice THESE TWO LISTS ARE NOT JOINED is literal: the two lists are separate readings. Captured media What this cockpit captured (photos, clips, voice memos) and what the platform said about each. Rules reconciliation engine The rules, with the checkboxes that bundle them for Simulate. See below. Readiness indicators What the agent rated on each domain, on its own 1–5 scale, category by category. A cell with no measurement says not measured. It never shows zero. Several sections also tell a failed request apart from an empty answer. For example, THE SOURCE LIST FAILED TO LOAD is a failed request, while NO SOURCES ARE CONFIGURED means the list was read and is empty. NONE REPORTED means the agent sent no indicators for a category. NOT MEASURED HERE means FACE does not compute that category.
data.set-a-rules-enforcement-and-send-rules-t: ### Open the policy editor In **Rules reconciliation engine**, select the tune button on a rule (**Open the policy editor**). The **Enforcement policy** drawer opens below it. Only one drawer is open at a time. ### Decide the posture Choose an **Enforcement action**: **Audit only**, **Review required** or **Block**. Optionally fill in **Tolerance** (in the rule's own units), **Policy reference** (the clause you are citing) and **Rationale** (why, for the reviewer). ### Save Select **Save policy**. It stays disabled until you choose an action. The drawer records who set the posture and when. If saving fails, **The policy was not saved** appears and your entries are kept, so you can try again. **Discard** drops your changes. ### Bundle rules Tick the rules you want to test. The chip counts them as **{b}/{n} bundled**. ### Dispatch Select **Dispatch reconcile posture to Simulate**. It bundles the ticked rules and their enforcement posture and opens [Simulate](/docs/cockpit/simulate/). The drawer also holds the Reconcile inspector. It is a read-only comparison of Actual — implementation against Intended — policy, with where the rule is implemented and what it is grounded in. Nothing to compare yet means FACE captured neither an implementation nor a policy for the rule.
data.the-maturity-verdict#The maturity verdic:
The banner states the result in one line:
Analysing your data domains… while the assessment runs. No data domains have been analysed yet. when the assessment answered with nothing. {n} domains analyzed · {n} findings across all domains · {n} measures to take on success, followed by Next: {measure} and a button for it. Plan remediation opens Compliance Remediation. Review trends opens a short explanation. Posture is unavailable — the reported reason is below. when the assessment failed. The server’s reason follows (Reported reason, in English:), with Retry. Could not refresh — this is the last result and may be out of date. when a refresh failed but an earlier result is still shown. The banner carries an AI-Generated tag when a measure was written by the model.
If no data source is attached, the banner is replaced by Nothing is connected yet, the instance’s own reply, and Connect a data source, which opens Connections.
The findings and measures themselves are listed on Twins.
data.two-views-of-one-estate#Two views of one:
A switch under the header chooses who the page is laid out for:
Executive briefing covers the maturity verdict, the relationships between domains, provenance, and the rules you bundle for simulation. This is the default. Operator deep dive covers the measured gauges, the live agent activity, and the detailed rules list. Old links still work. /rules and /ai_center?tab=rules open Operator deep dive.

data:
Each of the three domain twins has a detail screen that shows what it assessed:
Compliance Remediation (/compliance_remediation) Finance Remediation (/finance_remediation) Operations Remediation (/operations_remediation) To open one, go to Twins and select the chevron beside COMPLIANCE, FINANCE or OPERATIONS under ACTIONABLE TWIN STATUS. The tooltip reads Open COMPLIANCE, and so on. Plan remediation on Reconcile also opens the compliance screen. The back arrow (Go back) returns you to Twins.
The twins analyse the findings of your session fetch. The analysis runs automatically when a fetch completes, so these screens usually show a result already. Refresh runs the analysis again. It stays disabled until a session fetch has run, and its tooltip explains why.
data.could-not-look-or-found-nothing#Could no: You see Meaning Compliance analysis failed: {error} or Analysis failed: {error} The request failed. Unable to Assess, zero violations, and a grey banner The server answered, but it could not produce an assessment, for example because no connected data source was read. Connect a data source and run it again. No violations detected. or No findings detected. The twin assessed and found nothing. No compliance analysis available. No analysis has run yet. Run a session fetch first — this twin analyzes that instance’s real findings. No session fetch has run yet. Run one from Fetch.
data.rpcs-behind-these-screens#RPCs behind th: ComplianceService.AnalyzeCompliance. FinanceService.AnalyzeFinance. OperationsService.AnalyzeOperations. ComplianceService.AssignRemediation, DecideRemediation. ComplianceService.ListRemediationRoutes, SetRemediationRoute, DeleteRemediationRoute. See the API reference.
data.the-routing-table#The routing table:
On Compliance Remediation, Routing table holds your own map from finding category to department. FACE holds no org chart and proposes no route. A rule applies to future orders only. It sends nothing, and it does not re-address an order somebody already assigned by hand.
### Open Routing table Select the **Routing table** button in the title bar. ### Set or clear a rule Each category shows **RULE SET** or **NO RULE**. Enter a **DEPARTMENT**, a **CONTACT**, or both, then select **Save rule**. The server refuses a rule that names neither. **Delete rule** removes the rule, and findings in that category then arrive unrouted. A category marked **NOT IN THIS ANALYSIS** has a rule but no finding in the current analysis. You can still see and remove its rule here. ### Read the result **Rule saved.** or **Rule deleted.** confirms the change, and the rule records who set it and when. A message starting **NOT saved** or **NOT deleted** means nothing changed, and it gives the reason.
data.what-each-screen-shows#What each screen:
The verdict banner: the status the server reported, and how many violations or findings it counted. The live-data note: the server’s statement of which data the verdict rests on, word for word. The spoken summary. VIOLATIONS ({count}) or FINDINGS ({count}). Each item shows a severity word, its category and description, Remediation:, and the rule it was checked against (Rule:). AUDIT TRAIL: the systems that were checked, each with a status word and when it was last checked. The verdict banner has three kinds. Each has its own glyph, so the difference never depends on colour:
Banner Glyph Meaning Clear verified shield Assessed, with nothing to act on. Action required shield with a question mark Assessed, with violations or findings to act on. Unable to Assess (or another status that says it could not assess) question mark Not a verdict. Nothing could be assessed. The spoken summary gives the reason and says plainly that this is not a finding of compliance.
data.work-orders#Work orders: Findings can become work orders. On the finance and operations screens, each finding is followed by its order card, or by No work order was derived for this finding. What the records supported is the line above. The compliance screen tells you how many orders were derived. You work those orders under Remediation orders on Twins.

data: The cockpit opens on the sign-in page. Any page you open while signed out also brings you here, and so does a session that ends or that the server rejects.
data.choose-an-instance#Choose an instance:
An instance is the FACE deployment you are working in. The SELECT INSTANCE page (Choose an active instance to continue.) lists every instance your account has a grant on, under Choose an instance. The refresh button (Refresh instances) reads the list again.
Each card shows:
the product and the instance name; the tenant; your role: Admin, Editor, Viewer or Service account; the status; how long your access lasts, for example Access does not expire. A card marked Current is the instance you are already using. Anything the server did not report is shown as not stated, for example Role not stated.
Select a card to open it, even when it is the only one. The cockpit then starts a session fetch and a posture assessment for that instance and opens Fetch. Your role on the instance decides whether you see the Admin entry in the navigation.
data.rpcs-behind-these-pages#RPCs behind thes: IdentityService.Login: password, Google and the second-factor step. IdentityService.Logout. runink.ui.profile.v1.ProfileService.ListInstances: the instance list. See the API reference.
data.sign-in-methods#Sign-in methods:
When the page loads, the cockpit asks the backend which sign-in methods it offers. The backend answers on its /auth/config endpoint.
Method When it appears Email and Password Always. Google single sign-on Only when the backend reports Google sign-in as configured. An or divider separates it from the password form. If the cockpit cannot reach the sign-in service, the Google button is replaced by Single sign-on is unavailable — the sign-in service could not be reached. You can still sign in with your email and password. If the backend reports that it has no single sign-on, the page shows no Google button and no message.
### Enter your email and password Type your address in **Email** and your password in **Password**. The eye button (**Show password** / **Hide password**) reveals what you typed. Press Enter in the email field to move to the password field. ### Select Sign In Or press Enter in the password field. While the server checks your credentials, the button shows a spinner. Screen readers announce it as **Signing in**. ### Complete the second factor, if asked If your account has an authenticator enrolled, the cockpit opens the MFA page (see below). ### Choose an instance After a successful sign-in you land on **SELECT INSTANCE**. With Google, select the Google button and complete Google’s own dialog. A browser that is already signed in to Google may complete the sign-in without asking.
data.signing-out#Signing out: Sign out from your profile. Signing out closes any dialogs that were open and returns you to this page.
data.two-factor-verification#Two-factor verif:
The MFA Verification page asks you to Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator. Type the code into the six boxes. The code is submitted as soon as the last digit is in. Screen readers announce Verifying code while it is checked.
Cancel / Return to Login abandons the attempt. You can only reach this page while a second-factor challenge is waiting. Otherwise the cockpit sends you back to sign-in.
data.when-the-list-is-empty-or-fails#When the: You see Meaning What to do No instance grants you access — Ask an admin of the instance you need to invite you. The server answered and you hold no grant on any instance. Ask an admin of that instance to invite you. This deployment has no instances to choose from. The deployment itself offers no instances. Ask your platform operator. Could not be read, followed by a reason and Retry The list could not be read. This does not mean you have no instances. Read the reason, then select Retry.

data:
Simulate tests a hypothesis before anything is proposed for approval. Open it with Simulate in the bottom navigation (/simulate). The page has three tabs, in the order you would use them:
Tab For Link Metasearch Trends Searching the open web for a term, and checking text against the grounding rules. /simulate?tab=trends Causal Matrix The cause-and-effect structure found by the last simulation. /simulate?tab=causal Swarm Intelligence Running simulations and handing the results to Twins. This is the default tab. /simulate Older /lab links redirect here.
data.active-scenarios#Active Scenarios:
Panel Shows SWARM POPULATION One agent per inferred scenario, with the counts AGENTS, RUNNING, REPORTED, FAILED and STANDBY, and each agent’s state by domain. AGENT CONVERGENCE The nodes that more than one agent’s evidence named. Domain Nodes, Synapses, Open Rules Counts of each. ACTIVE SIMULATIONS Running scenarios with a progress bar. SIMULATION SCENARIOS below lists every scenario by domain. Tap a row to open that scenario’s detail page. SAVINGS SUMMARY The Total Identified Savings (USD) and a breakdown by category. The savings total tells four cases apart:
You see Meaning Measuring… Still loading. Not available The request failed. Nothing shown is a measurement. Not measured No summary has been requested yet. No savings identified in the current action set Measured, and the result was nothing. Could not load scenarios means the request failed. It shows the error and a Retry button. No scenarios yet means the list is genuinely empty.
data.causal-matrix#Causal Matrix:
The matrix is built from the evidence traces of the last simulation.
CAUSAL TOPOLOGY shows which node moves which, and how strongly. SUB-DOMAIN CAUSAL MATRIX tabulates the same links by SOURCE, RELATION, TARGET and SIGNIFICANCE. No causal evidence yet means no simulation has run. INTERVENTION sets one node and reads the effect on another. Pick Intervene on, enter Set to, pick Read effect on, and select Compute effect. The result shows EFFECT and NEW TARGET VALUE, and the note under it explains how the effect was computed. BAYESIAN POSTERIOR gives the posterior probabilities for a target node. Enter an observed state for any node, leave the rest blank, choose the TARGET, and select Infer posterior. The inference returned no probabilities means it ran and returned nothing.
data.metasearch-trends#Metasearch Trends: TERM SEARCH runs a live query against the sovereign metasearch engine. Type a term (Search a regulatory, market or operational term…) and select Search. Each result shows its host, its ENGINE SCORE (a ranking score, not a confidence), a snippet and Open source. No results means the engine ran and the web returned nothing. The search couldn’t run means it failed. GROUNDING GATE runs your text through the same OpenBias rules that guard the agent call. Nothing is sent and nothing is logged. Type the text and select Check this text. The verdict is Would be refused or No rule fired, with the number of rules evaluated. Show the {count} rules lists them. LONGITUDINAL TRENDS charts the forecast and anomalies from the last simulation. Until you run one, it says No series analysed.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: HypothesisService.GetHypothesisVariables, InteractiveSimulate (bidirectional stream), ValidateHypothesis, SendToTwins. AnalysisService.AnalyzeTimeSeries, AnalyzeDescriptiveStats, AnalyzeCausal, InferBayesian. MetasearchService.SearchTerms, EvaluateBias, ListBiasRules. TwinsService.GetSavingsSummary. ActivityService.SubscribeAgentActivity. See the API reference.
data.run-a-simulation#Run a simulation: ### Switch to New Simulation Select **New Simulation**. The parameters reset to the server's defaults. ### Choose the rules **SELECTED RULES FOR SIMULATION** lists the rules sent from [Reconcile](/docs/cockpit/reconcile/). You can also tap rule cards under **RULES CATEGORIES** to add or remove them. The × button (**Remove {name}**) drops one. If you select none, every extracted rule is used. ### Pick or name a scenario Tap a card under **SCENARIO CATEGORIES**, or type a name under **CUSTOM SCENARIO**. ### Set the parameters Under **Hypothesis Parameters**, move each slider (0–100%). The server supplies these variables. ### Run it Select **Run Full Simulation**. The button reads **Simulating…** while the run streams. Only one simulation runs at a time. **Save Scenario** keeps the scenario in this session without running it. ### Read the results **SIMULATION RESULTS GENERATED** is followed by: - **Model Confidence**, with a band: **High Reliability**, **Moderate Reliability** or **Low Reliability**; - any **ANOMALIES DETECTED**; - the **FORECAST**; - **SERIES DIAGNOSTICS**. Select **Analyse this series** there for descriptive statistics, stationarity and a recommended model. ### Hand it to Twins Select **Send to Actionable Twins**. **Queued for Twins** confirms the hand-off, and **VIEW IN TWINS** opens the queue. **No actions were produced by this run** means nothing was queued. **The handoff to Twins did not complete** gives the reason. The card is approved in [Twins](/docs/cockpit/twins/), not here. Live agent activity, at the bottom of the tab, streams every step the agents emit. It is the same feed as on Reconcile.
