If it is empty and the endpoint is http(s)://, generic_rest is used. endpoint A REST base URL, or host:port for NMEA. Required. asset_ids Restrict to these vehicles or assets. A query may narrow further, but only within this set. lookback_minutes Default 60, maximum 7 days collect_seconds The NMEA listening window: default 15 s, maximum 5 min include_sensors Also request reefer and cargo sensor channels where the provider has them property carrier / fleet Carried onto readings Credentials by provider:
Provider Credentials Samsara api_key, token or bearer_token Geotab database, username, password (or session_id) Generic REST bearer_token / token, or api_key, or username + password NMEA None Test: Samsara: one GET /fleet/vehicles/stats?types=gps&limit=1 Geotab: a Get of one Device Generic REST: one request NMEA: a TCP connect Execute returns position fixes as readings (latitude, longitude, geo_stated), with speed and heading in attributes. It also returns sensor channels where requested. At most 5,000 readings and 20 pages. Truncation is stated in the message. REST bodies are capped at 8 MiB. NMEA reads RMC, GGA and VTG sentences, with lines capped at 8,192 bytes. Units are taken from the provider (for example Geotab’s unit-of-measure ids) and never assumed. Explore returns supported=false.
data.mqtt-sensor-bus#MQTT (sensor bus):
Type spellings mqtt, mqtts, iot, iothub, sensorbus, messagebus, iottelemetry (iot_telemetry) Config message MQTTConnectionConfig, or legacy IoTConnectionConfig with endpoint plus a comma-separated topics property Protocol MQTT 3.1.1 (protocol level 4): CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH/PUBACK, PING, DISCONNECT Setting Meaning broker_url tcp://host:1883, tls://host:8883 (also ssl, mqtts), or a bare host:port. The default port is 1883, or 8883 with TLS. topics Topic filters. Required: an empty list is an error, and FACE never subscribes to # by default. A query can override the list with comma-separated filters. qos 0 or 1 (FACE subscribes at QoS 1). 2 is refused. client_id The default is a stable id derived from the connection id username A setting. The password is a credential. collect_seconds The listening window: default 15 s, maximum 5 min max_messages Default 500, maximum 20,000 protocol_version 4 or 0. 5 and 3 are refused with an explanation. use_tls, insecure_skip_verify TLS, and an explicit opt-in to skip certificate verification property asset_topic_segment The topic segment index that holds the asset id Credentials: password (also mqtt_password, api_key, token); username may also come from the bundle.
Test dials the broker and completes CONNECT/CONNACK within 10 s, then disconnects. It does not subscribe. Execute subscribes, listens for the window, and decodes each message: JSON objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and numeric strings become readings. When a JSON value names no metric, the metric comes from the topic’s last segment. Non-JSON payloads are kept as rows with payload_kind and a short sample. Topic, QoS and retained flags go into attributes. WebSocket transport, MQTT 5, QoS 2 delivery and persistent sessions are not implemented. A legacy iot connection that declares a non-MQTT protocol (such as AMQP) is refused by name. Explore returns supported=false. MQTT has no catalogue call.
data.rfid-llrp-and-vendor-rest#RFID (LLRP and:
Type spellings rfid, epc, llrp, tagreader Config message RFIDConnectionConfig Setting Meaning protocol llrp (default, also llrps) or http (also https, rest) endpoint LLRP: host or host:5084. HTTP: the reader’s event API base URL. reader_id Carried onto every reading. It defaults to the endpoint. location Where the reader physically is. It is carried onto every reading. antenna_ports Antennas to enable (1–65535). Empty means all. collect_seconds The inventory round: default 10 s, maximum 2 min max_reads Default 1,000, maximum 50,000 report_duplicates Report every sighting instead of first/last seen per EPC use_tls TLS. It is also implied by https:// or llrps://. property api_key_header The header for an API key (default X-API-Key) Credentials for HTTP readers, tried in order:
token → Authorization: Bearer api_key → the API-key header password with the username property → HTTP Basic Test for LLRP connects and waits for the reader’s connection-attempt event. For HTTP, it makes one GET to the event API within 8 s. Execute runs an inventory round and returns one reading per tag sighting. EPC, antenna, RSSI and read count go into attributes when the reader states them. HTTP event bodies are capped at 16 MiB, and an over-cap stream is refused rather than reported as a short round. Explore returns supported=false.
data.sensor-gateway-modbus-tcp-and-http#Senso:
Type spellings sensorgateway (sensor_gateway), sensor, modbus, temperature, infrared, thermal, probe Config message SensorGatewayConnectionConfig with one or more SensorChannel Setting Meaning transport modbus_tcp (default) or http. mqtt is refused here: use an MQTT connection, which emits the same rows. endpoint Modbus: host:502, or port 802 by default with use_tls. HTTP: a base URL. unit_id The Modbus unit (slave) id channels Required. There is no safe default register. collect_seconds The sampling pass: default 15 s, maximum 5 min poll_interval_seconds The interval between polls: default 5 s. It is carried as sampling_interval_seconds. use_tls Modbus/TCP Security, or HTTPS Each SensorChannel states its own mapping:
Field Meaning asset_id, device_id What is measured, and by which device metric temperature, infrared, humidity, shock, door or battery. It is written verbatim to the reading. address Modbus: the starting register. HTTP: the JSON path of the value. register_type holding (default), input, coil or discrete data_type int16 (default), uint16, int32, uint32 or float32. Word-swapped variants are accepted. scale, offset value = raw * scale + offset. A scale of 0 means 1. unit Written to the reading’s unit, for example C, F, %RH or g threshold_min / _stated, threshold_max / _stated, threshold_source The band the product spec states, and where it is stated. Leave these unset when nobody stated one. HTTP credentials: token, api_key, or username + password.
Test connects and reads the first channel. For HTTP, it fetches the document and resolves the first channel’s path. A failure names the channel, register and unit. A Modbus exception response is reported as the device’s own refusal. Execute polls every channel at the interval for the whole pass. The raw register and count go into attributes. Explore returns supported=false. Modbus has no register map, so the channel list you configure is the schema.
data.the-sensorreading-row#The SensorReading:
Every telemetry connector, and the Flipper edge reader, returns rows with these columns, in this order:
Column Meaning asset_id The thing measured, for example REEFER-12 device_id The thing measuring reading_id, window_id The reading id, and the monitoring run it belongs to reference, carrier Shipment or monitoring reference and carrier, only when the source states them observed_at RFC 3339, UTC observed_at_source Whose clock: device, gateway, or received (receipt time, used when the wire carries no timestamp) metric, value, value_stated, unit The measurement. value_stated=false marks a row with no numeric payload (a heartbeat, a door event, a tag sighting). Such rows are kept, because a gap in a feed is evidence too. threshold_min, threshold_min_stated, threshold_max, threshold_max_stated, threshold_source The band the source stated, and where sampling_interval_seconds The configured cadence. 0 means the source did not say. max_excursion_minutes, max_excursion_minutes_stated The excursion allowance stated by the spec load_reference, load_value, load_value_stated, load_value_currency The load on the asset, where named. load_value is money only with an ISO 4217 load_value_currency stated by the source; a load’s weight (load_weight, payload_weight, net_weight, a numeric load) never fills it and is kept in attributes as load_weight / load_weight_field / load_weight_unit location, latitude, longitude, geo_stated Where the reading was taken source, transport The connection type and the protocol actually spoken quality The source’s own quality flag. FACE never computes it. attributes Everything else the protocol knew, such as EPC and antenna, speed and heading, register and raw count, or topic
data.the-stated-fields#The \u003ccode\u003e*S:
In the protocol format FACE uses, “the probe read 0 °C” and “the row has no reading” look the same, and in a cold chain they are opposite facts. So every connector sets a *_stated flag from whether the source carried the field, never from whether the value is non-zero:
A threshold is never assumed. FACE does not assume 2–8 °C because an asset is called REEFER. A band that no one stated stays unstated, and analysis reports that the threshold was not stated. A unit that is absent stays absent. FACE never assumes Celsius. A position without geo_stated is not a position. Consumers must read a value only when its *_stated flag is true. See /docs/analysis/ for how these rows feed temperature-excursion and claims evidence.

data: These are the messages FACE connectors actually return, grouped by where you see them. An ellipsis (…) stands for a value the message fills in.
data.cameras-and-edge#Cameras and edge: Message Cause What to do cannot reach RTSP feed at …: … The camera did not accept a TCP connection Check the host, the port (554 by default) and the network path feed rejected the credentials (HTTP 401) Wrong camera credentials Re-enter the username and password device_capture is set but endpoint_url is also "…": choose one — … Both push and pull are configured Clear one of them unsupported image format "…" (only jpeg/png accepted) A pushed frame is not JPEG or PNG Send JPEG or PNG the Flipper agent at … is running but has no device: … The agent is up with no Flipper attached Connect and power on the device
data.connection-and-credentials#Connection an: Message Cause What to do Unknown connection type "…" The type matches no connector after lowercasing and removing spaces, underscores and hyphens Use a spelling from the connector pages. Google Workspace types (gmail, google_sheets, google_docs) are read by fetch only. Connection not found The id is no longer stored, for example after a stale list Refresh the list snowflake connection "…" has no password (or programmatic access token) in its credential store: … The credential bundle has no password, pat or token Re-enter the password in the connection form. A password on the record itself is never read. databricks connection "…" has no personal access token in its credential store: … No personal_access_token in the bundle Re-enter the token databricks connection "…" names no HTTP path: … http_path is empty Copy the /sql/1.0/warehouses/… path from the warehouse’s connection details ssl_mode "prefer" is not accepted: … (also "allow") These modes can fall back to cleartext Use require (the default), verify-ca, verify-full, or disable on purpose CREDENTIAL_STATE_ABSENT on the list This node holds no credential bundle for the connection Re-enter the credential. The state cannot tell “never entered” from “not on this node”. CREDENTIAL_STATE_UNREADABLE on the list A bundle exists but cannot be opened This is a key or storage problem on the instance, and re-entering the credential will not fix it. See /docs/operations/.
data.files-and-object-storage#Files and objec: Message Cause What to do missing S3 credentials: provide access_key and secret_key Incomplete bundle Add both keys bucket "…" does not exist at …, or these credentials cannot see it Wrong bucket, or no list permission Check the name and the policy reading objects is wired for S3-compatible stores only; "…" is not yet supported Reading GCS or Azure objects Use an S3-compatible endpoint for object reads no object key given: pass the key to read as the query Execute was called without a key Pass the object key as the query "…" is not an .xlsx/.xlsm file — use the CSV format for delimited text Excel connection pointed at another format Use an object-store connection for CSV
data.network#Network: Message Cause What to do refusing to reach …: it resolves to a … address, which is inside this deployment's own network … The connector refuses internal addresses by default If the source really is internal, set allow_internal_network=true on the connection refusing to dial …: that is the cloud instance-metadata service, not a data source. This refusal has no opt-in The address is the metadata service, directly or through NAT64 Correct the address. There is no override. refusing to dial multicast address … — a data source has one server Multicast target Use the source’s unicast address refusing to follow a redirect from … to …: … The source redirected to a different host Point the connection at the final host directly stopped after 5 redirects Redirect loop Use the final URL … returned more than N bytes: refusing to report a partially-read answer as a complete one — … The response exceeded the connector’s cap Narrow the request: a shorter window, a smaller page_size, one resource

Explore lists every route the installation declares. this connection carries a Guidewire username but no password. … The bundle has no password Re-enter it this SAP connection does not say where its OData service is, … No odata_url property Set odata_url to the service root, or sap_gateway_url to enumerate the Gateway’s catalogue SAP connector for system … cannot READ rows yet: … SAP row extraction is not built Use Explore for SAP metadata invalid ServiceNow connection parameters (systemUrl required) Missing systemUrl property Set it to the instance URL

Configuration saved — a live connectivity check isn't implemented yet for this source type

data:
FACE reads the web in two ways:
a web connection reads one configured page as rows of text the crawler service scrapes a page, or runs a bounded crawl from a seed URL
data.crawler-service#Crawler service:
CrawlerService exposes:
RPC Behaviour Scrape Reads one url and returns its title, main content and metadata. render_js is reserved. Crawl Starts from url and visits linked pages, returning a crawl_id, a status and pages_visited. GetCrawlStatus Returns the pages of a crawl: url, title, content_snippet and status for each. Crawl bounds:
url must be an absolute http(s) URL with a host. depth: 0 means the default of 2. The maximum is 5, and a negative value is refused. limit (pages): 0 means the default of 10. The maximum is 500, and a negative value is refused. allow_external: false by default. The crawl then stays on the seed’s host and its subdomains, on the same port. Only http(s) links are followed.
data.web-connection#Web connection: Type spellings webtelemetry (web_telemetry), webpage (the “Webpage” card), web, url, website Settings (properties) url (also endpoint, target_url, page_url, website, host) Schemes http and https only Internal addresses Refused by default. A page named by a URL is normally public. Set allow_internal_network=true to read an intranet page. Execute fetches exactly one page and follows no links: 30-second timeout, body capped at 8 MiB. At most 5 redirects, on the same host only. Only text and HTML are accepted. A document or image is refused, with a pointer to the file path. FACE extracts the readable text and splits it into chunks of up to 2,048 characters, with at most 400 chunks. Rows have the columns url, final_url, fetched_at, http_status, content_type, title, chunk_index, chunk_count, chunk_chars, content, truncated, source and transport. truncated is true when the body or the chunk count hit its cap. Test fetches the page, reading at most 64 KiB, within 15 s, and applies the same address and redirect rules. Explore returns supported=false. The connector reads one page by design. The request’s User-Agent is Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RuninkFACE/1.0) unless the operator sets SCRAPER_USER_AGENT.

data:
A model card describes one of FACE’s agents in plain language: what it is for, what it reads, what it hands a person, who has to approve it, which model it runs on, and where it stops. There is one card for each kind of work you meet in the cockpit. Several cards cover more than one agent, because those agents do one job together.
These cards are written for buyers, evaluators and operators. The mechanics behind them are on the Analysis & evidence pages, which these cards link to rather than repeat.
data.facts-shared-by-every-card#Facts shared:
Models. FACE sends each model call to one of three tiers on the deployment’s model plane, chosen by the kind of task (see Sovereign models):
Tier Base model in this release Maker Licence General reasoning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Qwen Apache-2.0 Code Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Qwen Apache-2.0 Vision (starts on demand) Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct Qwen Apache-2.0 Runink domain adaptation for each agent is planned. This release uses the base models as published by their maker. No card describes a trained or custom Runink model.
Not everything is a model. Many of the figures on these cards are fixed arithmetic over cited records: evidence documents, the dock triage of returns, forecasts, the approval policy. A model may phrase a result only after it has been determined. See Evidence documents.
Where inference runs. Every agent calls the model plane that runs inside the customer’s own deployment, on their Runink Server or in their cloud. FACE calls no third-party AI service. Records an agent reads are passed to the model as fenced, untrusted data, never as instructions (see AI safety). The connections you configure still reach their own systems, and an approved action, such as an email sent through a connected account, goes where that action says.
Guardrails. Each agent’s requests are checked against its OpenBias guardrail rules before a prompt reaches the model, and each proposed action passes the judging ladder. Both are described in Agents & oversight and AI safety, including what they do not establish.
Evaluation. No card has published evaluation scores yet. FACE claims no accuracy figure for any agent.
data.how-to-read-a-card#How to read a card:
Every card has the same sections:
What it does: one sentence, then the jobs it handles. What it reads: the records, documents and systems it takes in. What it produces: what you get back, and in what form. Human oversight: what a person approves, and what the agent can never do by itself. Model: the base model it runs on today. Where it runs and data handling: where inference happens. Guardrails: the policies it follows, in plain words. Limitations: what it doesn’t do, and when it declines or says data is missing. This is the card’s “what this does not establish” note. Evaluation: published evaluation results, when there are any. Some cards end with an illustrative example. Every name and figure in those examples is invented.
data.one-rule-for-every-card#One rule for eve: FACE drafts. A person decides. Every claim, short-pay, filing, order, quarantine, remediation and repair that an agent proposes is a recommendation for a named approver. Nothing is sent, filed, paid or settled until someone with the authority approves it, and the server records who did. The one exception is FACE’s own operational self-healing: restarting, isolating, rolling back or scaling FACE itself runs automatically from a fixed list, and an operator can switch it off. The approval tiers and the tamper-evident decision log are described in Auditability & lineage and Agents & oversight.
data.the-cards#The cards: Card What it helps with Base model Claims & recovery Shortage, OS&D and SLA claims, filing windows and the letter for approval. General Freight invoice audit Carrier invoices against the rate confirmation, SLA credits and spend. General Customs & trade documents Customs holds, document cross-checks and draft trade documents. General Compliance review Policy against practice, framework checks, personal data and remediation. General, plus code for code checks Insurance claim files Assembling the cargo claim file for an adjuster. General (documents use no model) Cold chain & telemetry Temperature excursions, sensor faults, site thresholds and custody. General Maintenance Equipment trending towards a limit its feed states. General Stock & demand Reorder decisions, forecasts and purchase orders for approval. General (forecasts use no model) Returns Return windows, quantities and disposition by your policy. General (dock triage uses no model) Yard & transport Yard capacity, border dwell, demurrage, custody and route ranking. General Hypothesis lab & approvals What-if scenarios and the approval tier for each action. General (approval policy uses no model) Field readings (edge) Writing up a handheld reader’s site walk. General Data posture Grouping your tables into domains and grading their readiness. General Voice dispatch Short spoken answers for drivers, with the call logged. General, plus the voice tier Documents & plans (vision) Camera frames, photographed forms and floor-plan images. Vision model, starts on demand Self-healing FACE’s own health: restart, isolate, roll back or scale, automatically. General Claims leakage Recoverable losses, credits and short-pays that never became a claim, handed to claims recovery. General Fraud indicators Patterns worth a reviewer’s look, with evidence and a likelihood band; never an accusation. General Freight market analyst Each lane against its own history and public fuel prices; re-bid and consolidation candidates. General Counterparty background check Public registry and sanctions findings on a carrier, shipper or broker, for review. Businesses only. General Customer analysis Cost to serve, service performance, claims, payment behaviour and concentration per business account. General

data: Agent: the claims leakage agent (claims_leakage in ExecuteLoop), with the CLAIMS_LEAKAGE evidence document and the ReviewClaimsLeakage call.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Never invents a figure. A missing amount is shown as not stated, never as zero. Refuses to inflate a recoverable amount or move a delivery date or deadline. Refuses to file, serve or deduct without the approver. Refuses to waive recovery against a favoured or related party. Each drafted step is checked by these rules as output, before it reaches you.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A claims handler or accounts-payable manager approves every recovery on the card it points to. Approval seals the evidence document; rejection needs a reason. The agent never files or serves a claim, sends a notice, takes a short-pay or deduction, or pays anything. A computed deadline is an input for the person deciding, not legal advice.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Invoice INV-208114: the rate-confirmation audit found USD 330 of accessorials the confirmation does not support. The payments ledger shows the invoice paid in full, USD 2,480, with no short-pay reference.
Draft. Short-pay not taken, USD 330 at stake. Recovery draft: the rate confirmation audit for INV-208114. Next step for the accounts-payable manager: review recovering the overcharge on the next payment run. Nothing has been deducted.
data.limitations#Limitations: It works from your records. A credit or payment that is not in a connected ledger cannot be seen, so “not received” is only reported when the ledger is connected. A concealed-damage window is calendared only when your terms state one. Identified money is not recovered money. Only what a counterparty pays back or credits is recovered.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The events, amounts and deadlines are fixed arithmetic over cited records. No model computes them. The agent orders the events and phrases the next step; the server copies amounts and handoffs from the card and drops any step that names a card, action or approver it cannot stand behind.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It finds money your own records show is recoverable and has not been recovered, puts the most urgent first, and drafts the next step for the person who approves the recovery. Its jobs:
Losses never claimed. A shortage or damage on the receiving record with no claim and no dispute file for the shipment. Claims not served. A claim on file where the correspondence shows no written notice sent to the carrier, with the filing deadline from the delivery date. Credits not received. Service credits an SLA audit computed, or credits a counterparty promised, that the credits ledger shows received short or not at all. Short-pays not taken. An invoice the rate-confirmation audit found overbilled that accounts payable paid in full. Concealed-damage windows. Goods signed for subject to inspection with no inspection recorded, and the notice window your terms state. Each event points to the recovery card that already drafts the claim: the OS&D report, the notice of intent, the rate-confirmation audit or the SLA audit. The claim is approved there, in the existing claims recovery flow.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A CLAIMS_LEAKAGE evidence document per event in the Twins queue, with the evidence bundle of the recovery card it points to, the amount at stake computed from cited records, and the earliest deadline with the rule that set it. From ReviewClaimsLeakage: the events due within a horizon you choose (past-due first), the total the cards state, and, if you ask, a drafted next step per event. Each step uses one of five actions (open the recovery draft, follow up a credit, review a short-pay, schedule an inspection, escalate to a claims handler) and names its approver.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Receiving (OS&D) records, the claims feed, dispute correspondence, carrier invoices with their rate confirmations, SLA scorecards, and two ledgers you tag as evidence sources: accounts-payable payments and credits. Where the ledger an event rests on is not connected, that event is not reported: a record nobody looked for is not evidence that it does not exist.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. Your records reach the model as fenced, untrusted data. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the claims agent (claims in ExecuteLoop), with the claims and recovery evidence documents.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Never invents a figure. A missing rate or document is named as missing, and no amount is given in its place. Does not decide or score claims on the basis of a claimant’s name, demographics or location, and does not lowball settlements for particular areas. Does not fabricate weather events or disruptions to build a force majeure defence. Does not build defamatory profiles of carriers, and does not scrape partner portals or private systems without authorisation. Stays on claims and recovery work; warehouse routing and macro forecasting belong to other agents.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A claims handler approves every claim letter, dispute and demand before it reaches a carrier. Approval seals the evidence document; rejection needs a reason. The agent never files a claim, contacts a carrier or withholds a payment on its own. A computed deadline is an input for the person deciding, not legal advice.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Load LD-482913, frozen fillets, delivered 2 March. Manifest gross weight 18,400 kg; weighbridge at delivery 17,860 kg. Contract rate on the delivery date USD 4.10/kg. Carrier claim window: 9 days from delivery. The consignee’s exception note is not on file.
Draft. Shortage 540 kg (18,400 − 17,860). Amount in dispute USD 2,214.00 (540 × 4.10). The window closes 11 March. Not on file: consignee’s exception note. A claim letter to the carrier is drafted and waits for the claims handler’s approval. Nothing has been sent.
data.limitations#Limitations: It works from your records. It holds no tariff, accessorial or market-rate tables, so a rate that isn’t in your contract file is reported as not stated. It doesn’t establish liability. A claim document assembles the file; the carrier, an adjuster or a court decides. A pattern that looks like return abuse is a lead for a person to check, not a finding of fraud. When a source could not be read, the document records the figure as absent with a reason, such as NO_BACKING_RECORD or NOT_STATED_ON_DOCUMENT.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The figures in the evidence documents (amounts, units, deadlines) are fixed arithmetic over cited records. No model computes them. A model may phrase the narrative only after they are set.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It puts a freight claim together from your own shipping records and drafts the paperwork for a person to approve. Its jobs:
Shortage at delivery. Compares the manifest weight with the weighbridge reading and the counts received, and works out what is short and what it is worth. Over, short and damaged receipts. Compares the purchase order, the bill of lading and the receiving count, and prepares the OS&D report. Filing windows. Works out the notice and suit dates from the delivery date and the named regime, and orders open claims by the earliest deadline. Disputes and recovery. Prepares the notice of intent to claim, the statement of position and the subrogation demand. Recovery procedures. Ranks the recovery work with the most money at stake first, for example SLA breach refunds, accessorial and duplicate-charge disputes, and return patterns worth a closer look.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Evidence documents from the closed vocabulary: OSD_REPORT, NOTICE_OF_INTENT_TO_CLAIM, STATEMENT_OF_POSITION and SUBROGATION_DEMAND. Each figure cites the record it came from, and each deadline names the rule that set it. See Evidence documents. Action cards in the Twins queue, each with one proposed next step, such as “send this claim letter to the carrier”. A short recovery plan: two or three procedures, ranked by money recovered, each tied to the records behind it.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Manifests, bills of lading, purchase orders, goods-received records, weighbridge events, carrier tracking milestones, SLA records, invoices and the business rules that Rules Recon found in your data. It can run read-only queries against the connection a run was started with. Other agents can hand it a sub-task with delegate_to_claims.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. Your records reach the model as fenced, untrusted data. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the telemetry agent (telemetry in ExecuteLoop), with the TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION and CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY_AUDIT evidence documents.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: No stated band, no breach. FACE never assumes a threshold the source didn’t provide, and never borrows an industry norm. A missing reading is “not measured”, never zero. A gap in the log is reported as a gap. Refuses to alter, suppress or fabricate sensor, GPS, speed, fuel or driver records. Refuses to bypass hazardous-goods segregation rules or crane safety locks. Refuses to run equipment control commands without a person’s authorisation. Stays on monitoring, cold chain, fleet telematics and yard safety.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A quality manager or supervisor approves every quarantine, reroute and release. The agent never adjusts a reefer controller, locks or unlocks a crane, stops a conveyor or reroutes a vehicle itself. It can propose a step or raise a cue as a request; a person acts.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Reefer RF-2207, band stated 2–8 °C, sampled every 15 min, 30 min out of band allowed. Readings: 06:00 6.1 · 06:15 7.4 · 06:30 8.6 · 06:45 9.3 · 07:00 9.1 · 07:15 7.9 · 08:00 7.2.
Draft. Out of band from 06:30 to 07:00, peak 9.3 °C, within the 30-minute allowance. Readings gap from 07:15 to 08:00: those 45 minutes are unknown, not normal. Proposed for the QA manager’s approval: hold the load and probe the core.
data.limitations#Limitations: A surface or air reading isn’t the product’s core temperature. The card says to probe the core; it doesn’t certify the product. Exposure is stated only when the records give the load value with a currency. Otherwise it is absent as “not measured”. Any projection of when a load will leave its band is labelled as modelled, not measured. An unrecorded handoff is not a break in custody. Custody findings are statements about the record, never about the goods or the people.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The excursion and custody documents are fixed arithmetic over cited readings. No model computes their figures.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It reads sensor and telematics data, works out whether a load really left its stated band and for how long, and drafts the quarantine, probe or reroute for a quality manager to approve. Its jobs:
Temperature excursions. Measures time out of the stated band, gaps in the log, and the load’s exposure when the records state its value. Sensor or product. Tells a stuck or silent sensor apart from a real change in temperature. Site thresholds. Flags speeding, perishable dwell at the dock and weighbridge differences against the thresholds your site states. Fleet and yard safety. Ranks events with a safety impact first, such as a hazardous-goods segregation problem or a driver in distress. Chain of custody. Finds intervals longer than the stated check-in cadence, door events with no task, and loads with no events at all.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Excursion and custody evidence documents, each figure cited. See Evidence documents. Action cards with a priority and one proposed step, such as “hold the load and probe the core before release”. Safety notices for a supervisor, ranked by urgency.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Temperature and humidity readings, reefer logs, GPS, speed, fuel and engine data, weighbridge events, custody events, dispatch states and the thresholds your records state. Telemetry arrives through the connections described in Telemetry. It can run read-only queries against the connection a run was started with.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agents: the compliance agent (compliance) and Rules Recon (rules_recon).
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Cites the source of every rule, and doesn’t invent files or policies. When nothing is found, it reports no rules. Reports no confidence score for its own verdict. The reconciliation status is the verdict. Refuses to create rules that discriminate, that retaliate against a particular employee, supplier or partner, or that bypass audits, governance checks or ethical sourcing obligations. Refuses to falsify emission figures or supplier ESG ratings, to weaken business continuity plans, or to bypass the personal-data masking and breach-notice triggers.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A person assigns, routes and decides every remediation order, and the server records who did each (AssignRemediation, SetRemediationRoute, DecideRemediation). Rule enforcement posture is set by an operator (UpdateRulePolicy). The agent can’t change a finding’s status that way. The agent never changes configuration, masking or data. Its remediations are steps for a person to take, such as a ticket or an escalation, never SQL or code fixes.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Rule Written policy Running system Invoice dual approval above 10,000 USD above 25,000 USD Perishable dwell alarm 4 h 4 h Supplier bank-detail call-back none required Access review every 90 days none Result. Dual approval: Drift. Dwell alarm: Aligned. Bank-detail call-back: Shadow. Access review: Missing. Drafted for the control owner: a change ticket to restore the 10,000 USD threshold, and a request to write the call-back into the SOP.
data.limitations#Limitations: It doesn’t certify compliance with any framework. A Pass is the agent’s reading of the evidence it was given. “Not assessed” is a separate result from “passed”. Where evidence is absent, the control is not shown as green. A breach-notice draft is a starting point for the data protection officer, not a legal determination. It gives no legal advice.
data.model#Model: Compliance and rule extraction: general reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Rules Recon code checks: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0) on the code tier. Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It puts what your policies say next to what your systems actually do, names where they part, and writes the next step in business language for the person who owns the control. Its jobs:
Rules Recon. Finds the business and governance rules in your data, documents, telemetry limits and code, and classifies each one: Aligned: the implementation matches the policy. Drift: both exist, but the implementation has moved away from the policy. Shadow: logic runs in the data or code with no policy behind it. Missing: a policy exists and nothing implements it. Framework checks. Gives an overall status of Pass, Fail or Warning against the frameworks you work to, and lists each violation with its rule and a remediation. Personal data. Flags unmasked personal data in reports, query results and logs, and drafts the masking proposal and the data protection officer’s notice. Emissions and supplier risk. Works out freight emissions with the method beside the figure, and summarises supplier compliance risk from the evidence provided.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A list of rules, each with its plain-English logic, the source it came from, its severity, its maturity (Low, Medium or High) and its reconciliation status. A compliance status, violations with a remediation each, and an audit trail of which systems were checked and with what result. See Compliance, finance, operations. Remediation orders for a person to assign, route and decide.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Policies, SOPs, contracts and SLAs; the running configuration and data of connected systems; logs and report extracts; telemetry limits; and, for Rules Recon’s code checks, source code and configuration files. It can run read-only queries against the connection a run was started with.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the counterparty check (counterparty_check), run from the Counterparty check tab of the Market & due diligence page.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Refuses a check on a private individual, or for a decision about a person’s credit, employment, housing or insurance. Refuses protected characteristics as a factor. Refuses to hide, drop or clear a sanctions match or a red flag. Never labels a business fraudulent or criminal and never blacklists it. Treats everything in a registry record or a list as data. It follows no link and no instruction found there, and a summary is withheld when the material carries one.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: The check decides nothing. A person reviews the findings and decides whether to work with the business. FACE does not block, reject, blacklist or notify anyone.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Check. Carrier, USDOT 4242, load valued at USD 150,000.
Findings. Authority first granted 30 days ago (red flag with this load value). Liability insurance on file: USD 0 thousand against USD 750 thousand required (red flag). Sanctions: one possible match on the OFAC SDN list, needs human review. EU and UK lists: not checked, the list download failed; the card says so.
Recommended. Review by the Compliance Manager before relying on this carrier.
data.limitations#Limitations: Registry data is what the registry published at the time shown and can lag reality. A clean result does not establish that a business is legitimate, and no name match does not clear anyone. FMCSA covers US motor carriers, brokers and forwarders. For a shipper or consignee those sources are marked not applicable. FACE does not search a registry by name. Without an identifier, that registry is not checked. SAM.gov results are marked “not verified against the live API” until one SAM.gov call has completed and been read on your deployment. Until then the result rests on SAM.gov’s documented response format. An answer FACE cannot read (an error page, an unexpected or partial response) is shown as not checked, never as “no exclusions”.
data.model#Model:
The findings are read from coded registry fields and computed on the deployment. No model decides them.
The optional summary uses general reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
data.not-a-consumer-report#Not a consumer rep: This is business due diligence. It runs on businesses only and has no way to name a private individual. It is not a consumer report, and it must not be used to make or support decisions about any person’s credit, employment, housing or insurance. A name match on a sanctions list is not an identification: only a person can confirm or dismiss it.
data.thresholds#Thresholds:
Each has a default and can be changed for a deployment, or for your organisation by an admin under Admin → Public registries & market data.
Threshold Default A new operating authority or company, younger than 180 days A high-value load (in the load’s own currency), at or above 100,000
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It runs business due diligence on a carrier, broker, freight forwarder, shipper or consignee from public registries and sanctions lists, and from your own history with that business. It produces findings for a person to review, never a rating. Its jobs:
Operating authority. Whether the US motor carrier or broker authority is active, and whether a revocation is pending. Insurance on file. Liability insurance against the required minimum, and cargo insurance or a broker’s bond where one is required. Safety and orders. The published safety rating and any out-of-service order in force. Authority age. When the authority was first granted. A very new authority on a high-value load is a red flag. Sanctions screening. The business name and the registered names against the OFAC SDN list, the EU consolidated list and the UK Sanctions List. Company registries. Legal name, status and registration from GLEIF (by LEI), SEC EDGAR (by CIK) and UK Companies House (by company number): an inactive or lapsed entity, a company in liquidation or dissolved, an insolvency history, a recently incorporated company, and a registered name that differs from the one given. Exclusions. Active SAM.gov exclusions (debarment or suspension), by Unique Entity ID. Your own history. Loads, on-time share, claims and disputes with this business in your records.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Findings, each with its source, a link to check it, and when it was retrieved. Red flags among them: revoked or inactive authority, insurance below the required minimum, an unsatisfactory safety rating, an out-of-service order, a very new authority on a high-value load, and any sanctions name match. Sanctions matches, always shown as a possible match that needs human review. Every source considered, including the ones not checked and why. At most one recommended action: a review by the Compliance Manager. The thresholds it applied.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: US FMCSA public carrier data (company census, licensing and insurance, authority history, out-of-service orders), by the USDOT or MC number you give. OFAC SDN list (U.S. Treasury), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (European Commission) and the UK Sanctions List (FCDO), downloaded in full and screened on the deployment. GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier records (CC0), SEC EDGAR company submissions (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission), UK Companies House company profiles (Open Government Licence) and SAM.gov exclusions (U.S. General Services Administration), each by the identifier you give. Your own lane history and account records. These registries were chosen because each is public, free, usable commercially, has an API keyed by an identifier, and registers companies. Where a registry can also hold a person (an LEI registered to a sole proprietor, an individual EDGAR filer), the record is reported only as such, with no name. Court dockets are not consulted. A source that is not given an identifier, or whose API key is not configured on your deployment, is listed as not checked with that reason.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. Registries are contacted only when an admin turns on Public registries & market data for your organisation (off by default, and separate from external web search). The only values sent are the identifiers you typed: USDOT, MC, LEI, CIK, UK company number or SAM.gov UEI. Sanctions lists are downloaded whole and screened locally, so the business name never leaves the deployment. SAM.gov and Companies House need a free API key, configured per deployment as a secret; the key is never shown, logged or passed to a model. Everything fetched is cached with its retrieval time. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the customer analysis (customer_analysis), run from the Customers tab of the Market & due diligence page.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Business accounts only. Rows that describe an individual or a consumer are excluded and counted, never analysed. Refuses to profile or track an individual person. Refuses to price or segment by protected characteristics. Refuses to inflate, hide or adjust cost to serve, margin, OTIF or payment figures. Recommends only. It does not send notices or terminate contracts.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: Every recommended action is a draft. Sending one for approval puts it in the approval queue, where a named person approves or rejects it. FACE does not change a price, send a notice or close an account.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Account ACME-12: 12 orders, revenue USD 12,000; activity costs stated on all 12, totalling USD 14,400 (transport USD 10,080, handling USD 4,320). OTIF 6 of 12. Paid on average 75 days after invoice.
Result. Margin USD −2,400 on costed orders. Suggested: a pricing review for the Commercial Pricing Manager, a service-level review for the Account Manager, and a payment-terms review for the Credit Controller.
data.limitations#Limitations: Cost to serve is what your rows state. Overheads your records do not allocate to orders are not in it, and a missing cost is never treated as zero. A churn signal is a pattern in your records, not a prediction that an account will leave. Days to pay is measured over paid invoices only. Concentration is computed in the currency with the most revenue; accounts in other currencies are not added to it.
data.model#Model:
The figures and the recommended actions are fixed arithmetic over your records. No model computes them.
The optional summary uses general reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
data.thresholds#Thresholds:
Each has a default and can be changed for a deployment, or for your organisation by an admin under Admin → Public registries & market data. Every result shows the thresholds it applied.
Threshold Default OTIF below which a service-level review is suggested 90% Days to pay above which a payment-terms review is suggested 60 One account’s share of revenue above which concentration is flagged 25%
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It analyses your shipper and consignee business accounts from your own records and suggests re-pricing, service-level and account reviews for a person to decide. Its jobs:
Cost to serve and margin. Activity-based cost to serve per account: transport, warehousing, handling, order processing, returns and other costs, as your records state them, with the margin on the orders that state both revenue and a cost. Service. OTIF (on time and in full) per account. Claims and disputes. Claim and dispute rates per account. Payment behaviour. Days from invoice to payment, weighted by amount, and open receivables. Concentration. Each account’s share of revenue, the top-three share and the Herfindahl-Hirschman index. Churn signals. Order volume falling, no recent orders, service levels falling and disputes rising, each with the figures behind it.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Per-account figures, with the number of rows behind each. Concentration figures and flags. Recommended actions, each naming who decides: re-pricing (Commercial Pricing Manager), service-level and account reviews (Account Manager), payment terms (Credit Controller), concentration (Commercial Director). On request, a short written summary. It phrases the figures above and adds none.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your own account records: one row per order, with the account, its type, dates, revenue, activity costs, delivery outcome, claims, disputes and invoice and payment dates. A connection is marked as account records by the operator. No public data is used.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called, and nothing leaves the deployment. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the documentation agent (documentation in ExecuteLoop), with the customs cards and the CUSTOMS_MANIFEST_EXCEPTION evidence document.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Refuses to falsify or fabricate HS codes, commercial invoices, packing lists or Incoterms to avoid a tariff or a check. Never invents a figure. A document or value that isn’t on file is named as missing. Duty is kept out of avoidable port charges, so a delay’s cost isn’t inflated.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: The customs or trade lead approves every next step and every document before it is sent or filed. The agent never files a declaration, submits a document to an authority or amends a manifest on its own. HS classifications are proposals. The declarant remains responsible for them.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Entry ENT-3308271, held for 6 days: certificate of origin missing for a preferential rate. On file: bill of lading, commercial invoice. Terminal demurrage USD 150 per day. Release checklist for this reason: certificate of origin, supplier declaration.
Draft. Held, 6 days. Missing: certificate of origin, supplier declaration. Port charges so far USD 900 (6 × 150), duty excluded. Proposed next step, for the customs lead to approve: request both documents from the supplier. Nothing has been sent.
data.limitations#Limitations: It gives no legal or customs advice. A computed date or limit is an input for the person deciding. A draft document is only as complete as the ERP record behind it. Missing fields stay empty and are named, never filled with a plausible value. It doesn’t check documents against an authority’s live systems. It doesn’t establish who caused a hold. It reports what the entry record says.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The customs exception document is fixed arithmetic over cited records. No model computes its figures.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It reads your shipping and customs records, finds what is holding a shipment up or doesn’t match, and drafts the next document or step for your trade team. Its jobs:
Customs holds. Finds entries that are held, which release documents are still missing, and the charges that have built up so far. Document cross-checks. Compares the bill of lading, commercial invoice and packing list for one shipment, and names where they disagree. Weight against manifest. When the weighbridge and the manifest differ by more than 5 %, drafts a manifest amendment. Draft trade documents. When an order is ready for dispatch, drafts the bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list and customs declaration from your ERP records, with the HS classification and Incoterm for review.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Customs cards with a priority and a proposed next action, such as “request the certificate of origin from the supplier”. The CUSTOMS_MANIFEST_EXCEPTION evidence document, with each figure cited. See Evidence documents. Draft document payloads (bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, customs declaration), an HS classification and the Incoterm, for a person to check.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Customs entry records, manifests, bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, weighbridge events, ERP order and shipping records, regulatory tables you provide, and the rules Rules Recon found in your data. It can run read-only queries against the connection a run was started with.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the posture agent (ai_posture), behind PostureService.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Builds the domain map from your schemas and samples. It doesn’t invent tables or domains. Refuses to inflate readiness scores or data-quality grades without evidence. Refuses to suggest or test dangerously open security settings, or to alter audit logs. Doesn’t penalise vendors or regions on assumptions rather than measured evidence. Stays on posture: fulfilment and claims belong to other agents.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: The data owner decides on every recommendation. The agent never changes schemas, masking or access.
data.limitations#Limitations: A grade reflects the structure of the data it could read, not how the data is used. A failed scan is an error, not a grade of F. A domain that couldn’t be read is not assessed, which is different from a pass. Business-meaning links between domains are the model’s inference. Check them before relying on them.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
FACE’s health score and letter grade also have a deterministic path that uses no model; Posture & maturity says which result came from where.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It reads your connected tables and documents, groups them into business domains, and grades how ready each domain is to be relied on, with the issues behind each grade. Its jobs:
Map the estate. Groups tables that share keys, entities or subject into domains, and names how each domain relates to the others, including links of business meaning where no key is shared. Grade each domain. Gives an A–F grade with six readiness measures (quality, risk, lineage, freshness, policy and cost) and the concrete issues driving the grade. Name the incidents. Writes up material data-maturity incidents with severity, impact, root cause, blast radius and a recommended fix.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A posture snapshot: domains, their relationships, a maturity scorecard and incidents. Results the agent wrote are marked as model-generated. See Posture & maturity.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Table schemas, sample rows and extracted documents from the connections you configure. Exploring a source never samples customer rows; reading rows is a separate, bounded call (see Data sources).
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. See Facts shared by every card.

data:
What it is: FACE’s image work: grading camera frames (Vision & CCTV), the vision agent (vision), reading photographed or scanned forms, and proposing elements from a picture of a site plan.
Runs on the Server’s vision model, which starts on demand. The first image request after a quiet period takes longer while the model loads. It is a general vision model, not yet tuned for forms or floor plans.
data.evaluation#Evaluation: No published evaluation scores yet. No detection accuracy is claimed.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: A person is not a subject. People never appear in the graded objects, and a frame with no inspectable object gets no grade rather than a low one. A detector’s class is never written into a graded label. Refuses to downgrade, hide or fake a camera assessment. Refuses to steer a sensor cue into unlocking a crane, blinding a camera or standing down a safety interlock, and refuses to plant false events into the shared operational picture. A model’s confidence in a value it read from a document is recorded, never used as a truth threshold.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: Nothing a vision model proposes from a plan is written to the twin graph until an operator confirms it. See Twin ontology & graph. A grade is input for a person. It never approves, rejects or releases anything. Any action taken on what a frame or a form shows goes through the same action-card approval as everything else.
data.limitations#Limitations: A grade and a damage percentage are the vision model’s estimate from downscaled pixels. They aren’t a physical inspection. Objects aren’t tracked between frames. A retained evidence frame shows the reviewer what was assessed. It isn’t a forensic, chain-of-custody record. It identifies no one.
data.model#Model:
The deployment’s vision tier: on Runink Server, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (Qwen, Apache-2.0), started on demand. It is a general vision model, not yet tuned for forms or plans; Runink domain adaptation for this work is planned.
The live camera view uses a local detector only and never calls the vision model.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It reads images and turns them into fields, grades and proposed elements that FACE and a person can check. Its jobs:
Camera frames. Grades the inspectable object in a frame: what it is, its material, a damage grade (PRISTINE, DAMAGED, DEFECTIVE or DESTROYED) and an estimated damage percentage. Optional detection draws one box per object of the graded class. Forms. Reads a photographed or scanned document, such as a bill of lading, packing list or delivery note, when text extraction alone can’t. Site plans. Proposes zones, docks and yard slots from a picture of a plan, for an operator to confirm.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A graded frame with per-object results, each box labelled with the stage that drew it, and notes that explain any absence. See Vision & CCTV. Values read from a document image, each recorded with the outcome of the read (READ, NOT_PRESENT_ON_DOCUMENT, ILLEGIBLE or EXTRACTION_FAILED). See Evidence documents. Proposed plan elements, which stay proposals until an operator confirms them.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Frames pushed to FACE or sampled from RTSP/HTTP camera feeds, document images, and plan images. Frames are downscaled before the model sees them.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane. No third-party AI service is called. Images travel in their own typed field, never as text inside a prompt. See Sovereign models.

data: What it is: the field-reading narrative, which writes up a walk with a handheld reader such as the Flipper edge reader.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Never computes, rounds, corrects or reconciles a figure. If two figures look inconsistent, it names both and leaves them unresolved. Never writes a reading with no value as a measurement. Never presents an ambient reading as support for the walk’s claim. An enclosure or device temperature measures the equipment, never the cargo, and the paragraph keeps that qualifier.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: The paragraph is a report. It proposes no action. Any action on a site walk is a person’s decision. It changes no figure. Every number in it is given to it and frozen.
data.limitations#Limitations: A sighting says a thing was heard. It isn’t a location, a count or an inventory. Radio occupancy says a band was busy, not what was transmitting. It doesn’t identify people or say whether anyone was authorised to be there.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The narrative records which model wrote it. The readings and their classification are set before the model is called.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It turns what a handheld reader picked up on a site walk into one plain paragraph that says what was found and, just as clearly, what the walk does not establish. Its jobs:
Phrase the walk. Writes one paragraph over readings that have already been decided, without changing any of them. Keep the distinctions. Keeps apart: a reading with no value and a reading of zero; “absent” (the sensor was driven and nothing answered) and “unstable” (something is there, but it isn’t a measurement); readings that support the walk’s claim and ambient readings taken at the same time; a gap (nobody was standing there) and an outage, which a gap never is. Say what it doesn’t prove. Includes the walk’s “what this does not establish” sentence every time.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: One short paragraph, with no headings, bullets, recommendations or next steps. When the paragraph can’t be written from the input alone, it says exactly what is missing instead.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: The frozen readings of one walk as the reader’s connector reported them, such as NFC, 125 kHz RFID, infrared, sub-GHz, 1-Wire and Wi-Fi sightings, with each reading’s role and quality, and the walk’s own statement of what it doesn’t establish.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. Labels from a field reader are treated as untrusted, because anyone nearby can influence what a radio reader hears. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the fraud indicator agent (fraud_detection in ExecuteLoop), with the FRAUD_INDICATOR_REVIEW evidence document and the ReviewFraudIndicators call.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: No profiling: it never uses or infers gender, race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, age, disability, a name, an address or a neighbourhood. Never looks into anyone’s private life, social media, family, criminal record or credit. Refuses to label anyone a fraudster or as guilty, and refuses to hold or deny a payment without a person. Refuses to hide or drop an indicator for a particular party. Each drafted check is screened against these rules as output, before it reaches you.
data.how-the-likelihood-band-is-set#How the l: Each check that agrees adds a fixed weight; statistics add theirs. By default a total of 4 or more is high, 2 or 3 medium, 1 low, and statistics alone never reach high. The statistics are a robust z-score and a two-sided CUSUM over a carrier’s own history, and a robust z-score of an account’s returns against other accounts. No model sets or moves a band.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A named claims or special-investigations reviewer decides each indicator, with one of two choices. Dismiss needs a reason, which is recorded. Escalate opens an investigation case for that reviewer. Both are written to the decision log. An indicator is never “approved”. The agent never accuses anyone, never holds, blocks or denies a payment, claim or refund, and never contacts the party named. An indicator is not for sending to the party it names.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Payment PAY-9 to a component supplier, USD 21,400, paid 12 September. The supplier’s bank details were changed on 1 September under change request VMC-0412; the ledger records no verification of the change.
Indicator. Bank details changed 11 days before payment; verification not recorded. Likelihood band: medium. Next check for the reviewer: call the supplier on a number already on file, not one on the change request, before the next payment run. No payment has been held. The reviewer escalates it to an investigation case.
data.limitations#Limitations: This is not a consumer report. It must not be used for decisions about an individual’s credit, employment or insurance. It works from your records. A pattern can have an innocent explanation the records do not show, which is why every indicator ends in a check, not a conclusion. With little history, the statistics do not run, and the band rests on the explicit checks alone.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The patterns, bands and amounts are fixed rules and statistics over cited records. The agent orders the indicators and phrases the next check; the server copies bands and amounts from the card and drops any step that accuses, names a card it was not given, uses an action outside its allowlist or names no reviewer.
data.review-thresholds#Review thresholds:
Every card states the thresholds in force and where they came from. The defaults:
Threshold Default Same payee, same amount: invoices this many days apart 7 days Bank details changed this many days before a payment 30 days Robust z-score at or above 3.5 Peer accounts needed before a return count is compared 8 Weight for a high band 4 Weight for a medium band 2 Highest band statistics alone can reach medium Weight of each check 1 to 4, per check Each one can be changed for your deployment. Set FACE_INDICATOR_THRESHOLDS_FILE to a JSON file that names only the values you change, for example {"version": "acme-1", "bank_change_window_days": 14}, or {"rule_weights": {"INDICATOR_RULE_BANK_CHANGE_NOT_VERIFIED": 3}}. A file that cannot be read or is out of range is not applied: the defaults stay in force and every card says the override was invalid.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It flags patterns in your own logistics and claims records that a claims or special-investigations reviewer should check, and drafts the check. It never accuses anyone. The patterns:
Repeated invoices or claims. The same invoice number paid twice, invoice numbers that match once punctuation is ignored, the same payee and amount within a few days, one load billed twice by one carrier, two claims on one shipment. Accessorial charges. The same accessorial billed twice on one invoice, or a charge far from that carrier’s own history for the same accessorial. Deliveries with no tracking presence. A signed delivery with no tracking record of the load on the delivery day, when the load or the carrier is tracked otherwise. Claims on clean deliveries. A claim against a receipt signed for the full quantity with no damage recorded. Carrier differences. The carrier on the rate confirmation is not the carrier on the delivery receipt or in the tracking feed. Bank detail changes. A payee’s bank details changed shortly before a payment, with no verification recorded. Return patterns. An account’s return lines far above other accounts’, or repeated returns of used goods, judged only against the returns policy.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A FRAUD_INDICATOR_REVIEW evidence document per pattern in the Twins queue: the checks that agree, each citing its records, a likelihood band (low, medium or high), the amount on the flagged records where one is stated, and one next check. From ReviewFraudIndicators: the indicators at or above a band you choose, and, if you ask, a drafted check per indicator. Each check uses one of six actions (compare documents, request a supporting record, verify a bank change by call-back, confirm the carrier, review the returns policy, refer to the reviewer) and names its reviewer.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Payments, claims, carrier invoices with their rate confirmations, receiving (OS&D) records, tracking telemetry and returns records. Everything is keyed by a business record: an invoice, a payment, a claim, a load, a carrier, a payee or a returns account.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. Your records reach the model as fenced, untrusted data. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the finance agent (finance in ExecuteLoop), with the rate-confirmation and SLA evidence documents.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Compares your invoice with your own rate confirmation, line by line. A rate the confirmation doesn’t state is reported as not stated, not disputed on a guess. Refuses to falsify cost-benefit, total-cost-of-ownership or cost-to-serve results. Refuses to fabricate or hide procurement spend to favour a vendor, and refuses to invent market-rate benchmarks. Stays on finance: claims disputes, dispatch, maintenance schedules and compliance audits belong to other agents.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: An accounts-payable or finance lead approves every short-pay, dispute and credit request. The agent never pays, withholds or credits money itself. Budget reallocations and procurement changes it suggests are recommendations only.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Invoice INV-208114. Detention: authorised, 7 h billed, 2 h free, agreed rate USD 75/h, billed USD 525. Lumper: not on the rate confirmation, billed USD 180.
Draft. Detention chargeable (7 − 2) × 75 = USD 375, so USD 150 over. Lumper not authorised: USD 180 disputed. Total USD 330. A short-pay dispute is drafted for the AP lead to approve.
data.limitations#Limitations: It doesn’t benchmark you against market spot rates. Its reference is your contract. Identified money is not recovered money. Only what a carrier credits or pays back is recovered. A transaction category comes with the agent’s confidence. It is a suggestion for your chart of accounts, not a posting. When the contract, the invoice line or the SLA clause is missing, the figure is reported as missing and no amount is given.
data.model#Model:
General reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
The audit documents’ amounts are fixed arithmetic over your invoice and rate confirmation. No model computes them.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It checks what carriers bill against what you agreed, and drafts the short-pay or credit request for finance to approve. Its jobs:
Invoice against rate confirmation. Finds accessorial lines that the rate confirmation doesn’t authorise, units billed inside free time, and rates above the one agreed. SLA credits. Works out the service credits owed under an SLA clause for late pickups or missed delivery windows. Order, invoice and bill of lading. Finds where the three disagree on quantity, and by how much. Spend oversight. Sorts transactions into categories with a stated confidence, flags spend that departs from its baseline, and compares options by cost-benefit, total cost of ownership and cost to serve.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Evidence documents RATE_CON_ACCESSORIAL_AUDIT (accessorials billed above the rate confirmation) and MSA_SLA_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT (service credits owed). Their headline amounts count as money only as described on Action cards & money. Action cards proposing a short-pay, a dispute or a credit request. For spend oversight: categorised transactions with a confidence, anomalies with the observed and expected values side by side, and recommended actions.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Carrier invoices, signed rate confirmations, master service agreements and their SLA clauses, purchase orders, goods-received records, invoice lines, the general-ledger chart you use, and the rules Rules Recon found in your data. It can run read-only queries against the connection a run was started with.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the freight market analyst (freight_market), run from the Freight market tab of the Market & due diligence page.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: The comparison is your own history plus public fuel data. It uses no proprietary rate index and refuses to make up a market or spot rate. Refuses to steer a re-bid or consolidation towards a favoured carrier. Recommends only. It does not book, tender, award or pay. A written summary that states a figure the analysis did not compute, or proposes an action outside its allowed set, is not shown.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: Every recommended action is a draft. Sending one for approval puts it in the approval queue, where a named person approves or rejects it. Approving records the decision. FACE contacts no carrier, sends no tender and awards no freight.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Records. Lane Chicago, IL → Dallas, TX. Last 90 days: 4 loads, median USD 2.40 per mile. The 275 days before: 6 loads, median USD 2.00 per mile. 5 of 15 tenders rejected.
Result. Rate 20% above the lane’s own baseline; flagged. A re-bid is suggested for the Transportation Procurement Manager to decide.
data.limitations#Limitations: A lane above its own trend is not proof it is above the market. FACE has no market rate for your lanes. The BTS index covers all US freight. It is context, not a lane benchmark. A fuel surcharge moving faster than diesel is a reason to check your contract’s fuel table, not proof of an error. A row without a linehaul rate, a distance or a distance unit is not used, and is counted with the reason. Nothing is filled in. With no network or no permission to reach the public sources, the lane figures still work; the fuel comparison is marked not checked.
data.model#Model:
The figures and the recommended actions are fixed arithmetic over your records and the public sources. No model computes them.
The optional summary uses general reasoning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen, Apache-2.0). Runink domain adaptation for this agent is planned; this release uses the base model.
data.thresholds#Thresholds:
Each threshold has a default and can be changed for a deployment, or for your organisation by an admin under Admin → Public registries & market data. Every result shows the thresholds it applied.
Threshold Default Lane above its own baseline by more than 10% Tender rejection share that flags a lane 20% Fewest tenders before the rejection share counts 5
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It benchmarks each of your lanes against that lane’s own history, and suggests re-bid, consolidation and fuel-surcharge reviews for your procurement team to decide. Its jobs:
Rate trend. The median linehaul rate per mile or kilometre over the last 90 days of a lane’s records, against the 275 days before. A lane above its own baseline by more than the threshold (10% by default), with enough loads in both windows, is flagged. Seasonal comparison. The same 90 days a year earlier, so a seasonal peak is not mistaken for a trend. Tender rejections. How many of your tenders on the lane were rejected. Fuel surcharge against diesel. How your fuel surcharge per distance moved against the US EIA weekly diesel price over the same weeks. Transit and accessorials. Mean transit days, on-time share against planned transit, and accessorial charges per load. Candidates. Re-bid candidates (above own trend, or many rejections), consolidation candidates (thin lanes from one origin to one destination region), and fuel-surcharge reviews.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Lane benchmarks with every figure, the windows they cover and the number of loads behind them. Flags with the figures that raised them. Recommended actions, each naming the Transportation Procurement Manager as the person who decides. The list of sources consulted, each marked live, cached, stale or not checked, with its retrieval time, and the rows of your records that could not be used and why. On request, a short written summary. It phrases the figures above and adds none.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads:
Your own lane history: the loads and tenders your systems record, with origin, destination, dates, tender outcome, linehaul, fuel surcharge, accessorials, distance and its unit, and transit days. A connection is marked as lane history by the operator.
Two public sources, as context:
US EIA weekly retail on-highway diesel price (U.S. Energy Information Administration, public domain). BTS Freight Transportation Services Index (U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, public domain), shown as national context only.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane, on the customer’s Runink Server or in their cloud. No third-party AI service is called. The two public sources are fetched only when an admin turns on Public registries & market data for your organisation (it is off by default, and separate from external web search). They are cached with their retrieval time; nothing from your records is sent to them. See Facts shared by every card.

data: What it is: the Hypothesis Engine (hypothesis), which runs the Hypothesis Lab in Simulate, and FACE’s decision-authority policy, which decides who must approve each action.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Every figure is worked out from the assumptions you state. When a discount rate isn’t stated, the default is shown. Refuses scenarios that assume one demographic group is superior to another, or that attribute failures to protected groups. Refuses scenarios aimed at price fixing, predatory or discriminatory pricing, market cornering or sabotage. Refuses to skew forecasts to influence orders or budgets, or to hide anomalies. Stays on analysis: booking freight or writing rules belong elsewhere.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: The Lab executes nothing and changes nothing in your systems. Sending a scenario to Twins is a separate act by a person. When no approval rule matches, the default is one named approver, never automatic. Safety and regulatory actions always need a person, and a dual approval needs two different people. Every decision is written to the hash-chained decision log before anything runs. If it can’t be logged, nothing runs. See Auditability & lineage.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
Assumptions. A second reefer lane: USD 240,000 up front; USD 110,000 a year in benefit and USD 20,000 a year to run, for 4 years; no discount rate stated.
